**ויען .** אלה ארבע רוחות. כמו לז' רוחי' . וכן ויבא ירושלם כמו לירושלם. ד"א לז' בן שחור כמו לבן שחור. והדומיו לו. לז' חלק הד' מרכבות ויוצאות לז' רוחות שמואל ב' י' השמים. כלז' לתת רשות לז' מלכיות למשול בז' רוחות כל אחת בזמנה . כלז' בכל העולם שהוז' ל' עזות : מהתיצב על אדון כל הארץ. כלז' בשליחות האל ששלטם על זה . כמו עומר ויבחו בני האלהים להתיצב על ה' : <margin>איוב ב'</margin> **אשר בה .** השחורים . ולז' זכר השחורים כי כבר עבר עתק מלכות בבל . ומלכות מדי ופרס יחיו תחלה אל ארץ צפון שהיו בכל להשחיתה וחח"כ משלו בכל ממלכות הארץ: והלבני' שהוז' מלכות יון יצאו אל אחריה' שהמלכות נברק . שהיו אלכסנדרוס מקדון המלך הראשון ליון הרג דריוש בבבל ולקח המלוכה ממנו ומלך וח"כ קוז וקכחיס חחריו בכל העולם : **והברודי' יצאו אל ארץ התימן .** שהיו חלק קדוס כעבור כי רומי היא שנונית ויוכיחום קיסר שמלך על רומי החל להלחם במלכות יון ובתחילת מלחמותיו יצא אל ארץ מצרים שהיא דרומית ובכל הארצות היו מולכים בני יון חז . וזק ויוכיחום קיסר התגבר עליהם והוז' העביר המלוכה מבני יון והחזירה לרומיים : **והאמוצים .** הם רמז למלכות ישמעאל שהתחמט מעצמם לבקש מלוכה לחיות מקום שיהיה לשיכך לז' קתר להם רוח . וזהו שאמר ויבקשו ללכת להתהלך בארץ : **ויאמר .** כלומר נתן להם רשות להתהלך ולכבוש ארצות : **ויזעק .** כלומ' קרא עלי בקול גדול וחמר לי **ראה היוצאים אל ארץ צפון הניחו את רוחי בארץ צפון** כלומר חלק השחורים שיצאו אל בבל להשחיתה

I have already seen that the visions represent the four monarchies; if so, what are these? for what purpose do I see them?
“And the angel answered ——— These the four winds of heaven”—Winds רוחות here signifies the same as לרוחות to the winds. (There are similar cases where the preposition ל, to, is omitted,) as ויבא ירושלם, “And he came Jerusalem,” i.e., to Jerusalem. (1 Kings iii. 15.) And again: בן שאול, “the son of Saul,” for לבן שאול, “to the son of Saul” (2 Sam. iv. 2); and other similar cases. The meaning is, These four chariots go forth to the four winds of heaven; i.e., to give permission to the four monarchies to rule in the four winds, each in its time, that is to say, in the whole world, which has four corners.
“From standing before the Lord of the whole earth,” i.e., commissioned by God, who sent them, according as it is said, “And the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord.” (Job i. 6.)
“Which are therein.”—He does not mention the red horses, for the Babylonian monarchy had already passed away. The Medo-Persian monarchy went forth first to the land of the north, which is Babylon, to destroy it, but afterwards ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. The white horses, which represent the Grecian monarchy, went forth after them, when their kingdom was strong; for behold, Alexander the Macedonian, the first King of Greece, slew Darius in Babylon, and took the kingdom from him, and afterwards had dominion, he and his successors, over the whole earth.
“And the grisled go forth toward the country of Teman,” which is the south country, for Rome is to the north, and Lulianus Cæsar, who reigned over Rome, began to wage war against the kingdom of Greece; and in the beginning of his wars, he went forth to the land of Egypt, which is to the south. At that time the Greeks ruled over all lands, but this Lulianus Cæsar prevailed against them, and caused the kingdom to pass away from the Greeks, and turned it to the Romans.
“And the bay” (strong).—These signify the Turkish empire, who strengthened themselves to seek a kingdom in any place that might offer: and therefore he does not define any wind of heaven for them. This is what is said, “And they sought to go, that they might walk to and fro through the earth.”
“And he said,” i.e., Permission was given them to walk to and fro, and to subdue lands.
“Then cried he upon me.”—He cried upon me with a loud voice, and said to me, “Behold these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country; i.e., These black horses which went forth to Babylon to destroy it
[context] have caused a quieting of my spirit by destroying it.

# Zechariah

For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are a hint to the seven <note>likely a scribal error or variant for four</note> kingdoms. And the meaning of "What are these?" is to give life to my understanding of them:

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses is going out to the north country, and the white ones have gone out after them, and the dappled ones have gone out to the south country." And the strong ones went out and sought to go, to walk to and fro through the earth; and he said, "Go, walk to and fro through the earth." So they walked to and fro through the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those who go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."

**And he answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like saying "for the four winds." Similarly, "and he came to Jerusalem" is like saying "into Jerusalem." Alternatively, it is like "white-black" meaning "towards white-black" and its equivalents. This refers to the division of the four chariots going out to the four winds of the heavens. This is to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each one in its time. This refers to the whole world, which is a term for strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth." This means they act as messengers of God, who gave them dominion over this. It is like the verse, "the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**The one with.** "The black ones." He mentions the black ones first <note>referring to the second chariot in the vision sequence</note> because the era of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia went first to the north country, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white ones," which refers to the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them" once the kingdom was established. For Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingship from him and reigned; and afterward his successors ruled throughout the whole world.

**And the dappled ones went out to the south country.** These represent the Roman portion, because Rome is <unclear>shnunith</unclear>. This is proven by the Caesar who ruled over Rome; he began to fight against the Greek kingdom, and at the start of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks were ruling in all lands. That Caesar prevailed over them, and he transferred the kingship from the Greeks and restored it to the Romans.

**And the strong ones.** These are a hint to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>The Islamic Caliphate</note> who incited themselves to seek kingship, to find a place that would be for <unclear>their power</unclear>. This is what is meant by "and they sought to go, to walk to and fro through the earth."

**And he said.** This means He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me, **"See, those who go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the portion of the black horses that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>A commentary on Zechariah 6 describing the vision of the four chariots as a metaphor for the succession of historical empires: Persia, Greece, Rome, and the Islamic Caliphate.</summary>

### Zechariah

For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are an allusion to the seven kingdoms <note>The commentator links the four chariots to various ruling powers in history</note>. And likewise: "What are these?" <note>referring to Zechariah 6:4</note> refers to the matter of my living among them.

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going forth from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes forth to the north country, and the white ones go forth after them, and the dappled ones go forth to the south country." And the strong ones went forth and sought to go, to walk about through the earth; and he said, "Go, walk about through the earth." So they walked about through the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those who go forth to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country." <note>Zechariah 6:5–8</note>

**And he answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like "to the seven winds." Similarly, "and he came to Jerusalem" is like "unto Jerusalem." Another interpretation: "unto the son of Shachor" is like "to the son of Shachor," and similar cases. This refers to the division of the four chariots, and they go out to the seven directions of the heavens. This is to give permission to the seven kingdoms to rule in the seven directions, each one in its time, throughout the whole world, which is characterized by boldness. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth." This refers to the mission from God who gave them dominion over this, as it is written: "The sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**The one with.** The black ones. He mentions the black ones because the time of the Kingdom of Babylon had already passed. The Kingdom of Media and Persia <note>historical successors to Babylon</note> went first to the north country, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth.

And the white ones, which are the Kingdom of Greece <note>the empire of Alexander the Great</note>, went out after them once that kingdom was established. Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he ruled, and afterward his successors ruled throughout the entire world.

**And the dappled ones went forth to the south country.** This refers to the Roman portion, because Rome is <unclear>shnunith</unclear>. This is proven by Caesar, who ruled over Rome and began to fight against the Kingdom of Greece. At the start of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south, and at that time the Greeks were ruling in all those lands. But Caesar prevailed over them and transferred the kingdom from the Greeks, returning it to the Romans.

**And the strong ones.** These are an allusion to the Kingdom of Ishmael <note>the Islamic conquests</note> who incited themselves to seek a kingdom, to find a place for themselves where they would have spirit. This is why it says, "and they sought to go, to walk about through the earth."

**And he said.** That is to say, He gave them permission to walk about and to conquer lands.

**Then he cried out.** That is to say, he called to me with a great voice and said to me: **"See, those who go forth to the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the portion of the black horses that went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>A commentary on Zechariah 6 interpreting the four chariots as the successive empires of Media-Persia, Greece, Rome, and the Islamic conquests. It identifies Alexander the Great and the Roman Caesars as agents of these shifts in global power.</summary>

The angel answered and said to me: These are the four spirits of the heavens, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses goes out to the land of the north; and the white ones went out after them; and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying: "Behold, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."

**And he answered.** "These are the four spirits." This is like "to the four spirits." And similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" <note>original: "ויבא ירושלם"</note> is like "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: "to the four" <note>clarification: explaining the prepositional use</note>, like "son of Shahor" is like "to the son of Shahor," and those similar to it. To the four divisions of the four chariots, and they go out to the four spirits <note>clarification: directions</note> of the heavens. All this is to give authority to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time. All this is in the whole world, which is the meaning of strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth" <note>original: "מהתיצב על אדון כל הארץ"</note>. This means by the mission of God who gave them dominion over this. Just as it says: "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**In which.** "The black." And he did not mention the first <note>clarification: the first chariot/horses</note> because the time of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. And the kingdom of Media and Persia went out first to the land of the north, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white ones," which are the kingdom of Greece, "went out after them" because that kingdom was established <note>alternative: or "cleared"</note>. For Alexander of Macedon <note>term</note> <gloss>Alexander the Great</gloss>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingship from him and reigned; and afterward his successors <note>unclear>קוז וקכחיס</note> reigned after him in the whole world.

**And the dappled ones went out to the land of the south.** For they were the portion of <unclear>קדוס</unclear> because Rome is <unclear>שנונית</unclear>. And <term>Augustus</term> <gloss>Octavian</gloss> Caesar, who reigned over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece; and at the beginning of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is southern. And in all the lands, the sons of Greece were then ruling. And <term>Augustus</term> Caesar prevailed over them and transferred the kingship from the sons of Greece and returned it to the Romans.

**And the strong ones.** They are an allusion to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>context: traditional rabbinic identification for the Islamic Caliphate/Arabs</note> who exerted themselves <note>clarification: or "strengthened themselves"</note> on their own to seek kingship, to find a place to dwell, for there was a spirit granted to them. And this is what it says: "And they sought to go, to walk about the earth."

**And he said.** That is to say, he gave them permission to walk about and to conquer lands.

**And he cried out.** That is to say, he called to me with a great voice and said to me: **"Behold, those who go out to the land of the north have set my spirit at rest in the land of the north."** That is to say, the portion of the black ones who went out to Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>A commentary on Zechariah 6 explaining the vision of the four chariots and horses as symbols for historical empires: Media-Persia, Greece, Rome, and the Arabs.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four spirits, Babylon, Media, Persia, Greece, Rome, Ishmael, Alexander the Great, Augustus Caesar</keywords>

For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are an allusion to the seven kingdoms. And so, "What are these" <note>clarification: referring to the horses in the vision</note> is a matter of my life within them.

The angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes out toward the north country, and the white horses go out after them, and the dappled horses go out toward the south country." Then the strong horses went out and sought to go and walk to and fro throughout the earth, and he said, "Go, walk to and fro throughout the earth." So they walked to and fro throughout the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those who go toward the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country."

**The angel answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like saying "to the four winds." Similarly, "and he came Jerusalem" is like "to Jerusalem." Another interpretation: the letter <term>bet</term> in "with the black" <note>original: "בשחור"</note> is like the letter <term>lamed</term>, "to the black," and similar cases. This means He divided the four chariots and they go out to the four winds of heaven. This is to give authority to the four kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each one in its own time. This refers to the whole world, which is a place of strength. "From standing before the Lord of all the earth." This means they go as messengers of God, who gave them dominion over this. It is like the verse, "The sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

**The one with.** The black horses. He mentions the black ones because the time of the kingdom of Babylon had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia first went toward the north country, as they were meant to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white horses," which are the kingdom of Greece <note>original: "מלכות יון"</note>, went out after them as that kingdom emerged. For Alexander of Macedon <note>original: "אלכסנדרוס מקדון"</note>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him, and he and the kings after him ruled throughout the entire world.

**And the dappled horses go out toward the south country.** This refers to the Roman part <note>clarification: the Roman Empire</note>, for Rome is in the north, as proven by the Caesar who ruled over Rome. He began to fight against the kingdom of Greece, and at the beginning of his wars, he went out toward the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks ruled in all lands, but Caesar grew strong against them and transferred the kingdom from the Greeks and restored it to the Romans.

**And the strong horses.** These are an allusion to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>context: traditionally identified with the Islamic Caliphates</note>, who exerted themselves of their own accord to seek a kingdom, to find a place for themselves to settle. This is why it says, "and they sought to go and walk to and fro throughout the earth."

**And he said.** Meaning, He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me: **"See, those who go toward the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the black horses that went out toward Babylon to destroy it.

<summary>This page contains a commentary on the vision of the four chariots from Zechariah 6, interpreting the colored horses as the historical kingdoms of Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and Ishmael.</summary>
<keywords>Zechariah, four winds, Media and Persia, Greece, Alexander the Great, Rome, Ishmael, Babylon</keywords>

בצדן בשובו אל נותן כתיב: כי עין בעין יראו בשוב ה' ציון: ואמר ונגלה כבוד ה' וראו כל בשר יחדו כי פי ה' דבר: אב הרחמים הוא ינחם עם עמוסים ויזכור ברית איתנים ויציל נפשותינו מן השעות הרעות ויגער ביצר הרע מן הנשאים ויחון אותנו לפליטת עולמים. וימלא משאלותינו במדת טובה ישועה ורחמים:

<image-desc size="small" type="decorative" significance="low">Decorative ornament</image-desc>

כסא דנביאין ספר מורא חופים וכו':
ואת התורה אשר שם משה לפני בני ישראל על פי ה' ביד משה:

הללו את שם ה' כי נשגב שמו לבדו:
הודו על ארץ ושמים: וירם קרן לעמו תהלה לכל חסידיו לבני ישראל עם קרובו הללויה:

ואומר בשם עומד לדור, וכתוב ול"מ ויו"ם ובזמן כנמנה לדור מעור.
כסא דנביאין פס"ק (כיכל חופים וכו'):

ובטחה ואמר שובה ה' רבבות אלפי ישראל: קומה ה' למנוחתך אתה וארון עזך: כהניך ילבשו צדק וחסידיך ירננו: בעבור דוד עבדך אל תשב פני משיחך: כי לקח טוב נתתי לכם תורתי אל תעזובו: עץ חיים היא למחזיקים בה ותומכיה מאשר: דרכיה דרכי נועם וכל נתיבותיה שלום: השיבנו ה' אליך ונשובה חדש ימינו כקדם: אשרי וכו':

למנצח מזמור לדוד: יענך ה' ביום צרה ישגבך שם אלהי יעקב: ישלח עזרך מקדש ומציון יסעדך: יזכור כל מנחותיך ועולתך ידשנה סלה: יתן לך כלבבך וכל עצתך ימלא: נרננה בישועתך ובשם אלהינו נדגול ימלא ה' כל שאלותיך: עתה ידעתי כי הושיע ה' משיחו יענהו משמי קדשו בגבורות ישע ימינו: אלה ברכב ואלה בסוסים ואנחנו בשם ה' אלהינו נזכיר: המה כרעו ונפלו ואנחנו קמנו ונתעודד: ה' הושיעה המלך יעננו ביום קראנו: ואני לציון גואל ולשבי פשע ביעקב נאם ה': ואני זאת בריתי אותם אמר ה' רוחי אשר עליך ודברי אשר שמתי בפיך לא ימושו מפיך ומפי זרעך ומפי זרע זרעך אמר ה' מעתה ועד עולם:

ואתה קדוש יושב תהלות ישראל: וקרא זה אל זה ואמר קדוש קדוש קדוש ה' צבאות מלא כל הארץ כבודו: ומקבלים דין מן דין ואמרין קדיש בשמי מרומא עלאה בית שכינתיה קדיש על ארעא עובד גבורתיה קדיש לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: ה' צבאות מליא כל ארעא זיו יקריה: נהשאנא רוח נשמע אהקיל רעש גדול רב רבין כבוד ה' ממקומו: ונשפתני רוחא ושמעת בתרי קל זיע סגיא דמשבחין ואמרין קריה יקרא דיו מאתר בית שכינתיה: ה' לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יי מלכותיה קאם לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יי אלהי אברהם יצחק וישראל אבותינו שמרה זאת לעולם ליצר מחשבות לבב עמך והכן לבבם אליך: והוא רחום יכפר עון ולא ישחית והרבה להשיב אפו ולא יעיר כל חמתו: כי אתה אדני טוב וסלח ורב חסד לכל קוראיך: צדקתך צדק לעולם ותורתך אמת: תתן אמת ליעקב חסד לאברהם אשר נשבעת לאבותינו מימי קדם: ברוך אדני יום יום יעמס לנו האל ישועתנו סלה: ה' צבאות עמנו משגב לנו אלהי יעקב סלה: ה' צבאות אשרי אדם בוטח בך: ה' הושיעה המלך יעננו ביום קראנו: ברוך הוא אלהינו שבראנו לכבודו והבדילנו מן התועים ונתן לנו תורת אמת וחיי עולם נטע בתוכנו הוא יפתח לבנו בתורתו וישם בלבבנו אהבתו ויראתו ולעשות רצונו ולעבדו בלבב שלם למען לא ניגע לריק ולא נלד לבהלה: יהי רצון מלפניך ה' אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו שנשמור חקיך בעולם הזה ונזכה ונחיה ונראה ונירש טובה וברכה לשני ימות המשיח ולחיי העולם הבא: למען יזמרה כבוד ולא ידום ה' אלהי לעולם אודך: ברוך הגבר אשר יבטח בה' והיה ה' מבטחו: בטחו בה' עדי עד כי ביה ה' צור עולמים: ויבטחו בך יודעי שמך כי לא עזבת דורשיך ה': חפץ למען צדקו יגדיל תורה ויאדיר:

<column-break/>

יי אדונינו מה אדיר שמך בכל הארץ:
חוקו ויאמץ לבבכם כל המיחלים ליי:

ועתה יגדל נא כח אדני כאשר דברת לאמר: זכור רחמיך וחסדיך כי מעולם המה:

יתגדל ויתקדש שמה רבא. בעלמא די ברא כרעותה וימליך מלכותיה ויצמח פורקניה ויקרב [נ"א קץ] משיחיה: בחייכון וביומיכון ובחיי דכל בית ישראל בעגלא ובזמן קריב ואמרו אמן: יהא שמה רבא מברך לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יתברך וישתבח ויתפאר ויתרומם ויתנשא ויתהדר ויתעלה ויתהלל שמה דקודשא בריך הוא. לעילא (מפע"ם ולעילא מכל) מן כל ברכתא ושירתא תשבחתא ונחמתא דאמירן בעלמא ואמרו אמן: קבל קבל ברחמים וברצון את תפלתנו: תתקבל צלותהון ובעותהון דכל בית ישראל קדם אבוהון די בשמיא ואמרו אמן: קבל יהי שם ה' מבורך מעתה ועד עולם:

מן יהא שלמא רבא מן שמיא וחיים עלינו ועל כל ישראל ואמרו אמן: קסו עזרי מעם ה' עשה שמים וארץ: עשה שלום במרומיו הוא יעשה שלום עלינו ועל כל ישראל ואמרו אמן:

תפלה לדוד הטה ה' אזנך עני כי עני ואביון אני: שמרה נפשי כי חסיד אני הושיע עבדך אתה אלהי הבוטח אליך: חנני אדני כי אליך אקרא כל היום: שמח נפש עבדך כי אליך אדני נפשי אשא: כי אתה אדני טוב וסלח ורב חסד לכל קוראיך: האזינה ה' תפלתי והקשיבה בקול תחנוני: ביום צרתי אקראך כי תענני: אין כמוך באלהים אדני ואין כמעשיך: כל גוים אשר עשית יבואו וישתחוו לפניך אדני ויכבדו לשמך: כי גדול אתה ועושה נפלאות אתה אלהים לבדך: הורני ה' דרכך אהלך באמתך יחד לבבי ליראה שמך: אודך אדני אלהי בכל לבבי ואכבדת שמך לעולם: כי חסדך גדול עלי והצלת נפשי משאול תחתיה: אלהים זדים קמו עלי ועדת עריצים בקשו נפשי ולא שמוך לנגדם: ואתה אדני אל רחום וחנון ארך אפים ורב חסד ואמת: פנה אלי וחנני תנה עזך לעבדך והושיעה לבן אמתך: עשה עמי אות לטובה ויראו שנאי ויבשו כי אתה ה' עזרתני ונחמתני:

בית יעקב לכו ונלכה באור יי: כי כל העמים ילכו איש בשם אלהיו ואנחנו נלך בשם ה' אלהינו לעולם ועד:
יהי ה' אלהינו עמנו כאשר היה עם אבותינו אל יעזבנו ואל יטשנו: להטות לבבנו אליו ללכת בכל דרכיו ולשמור מצותיו וחקיו ומשפטיו אשר צוה את אבותינו: ויהיו דברי אלה אשר התחננתי לפני ה' קרובים אל ה' אלהינו יומם ולילה לעשות משפט עבדו ומשפט עמו ישראל דבר יום ביומו: למען דעת כל עמי הארץ כי ה' הוא האלהים אין עוד:

שיר המעלות לדוד לולי ה' שהיה לנו יאמר נא ישראל: לולי ה' שהיה לנו בקום עלינו אדם: אזי חיים בלעונו בחרות אפם בנו: אזי המים שטפונו נחלה עבר על נפשנו: אזי עבר על נפשנו המים הזדונים: ברוך ה' שלא נתננו טרף לשניהם: נפשנו כצפור נמלטה מפח יוקשים הפח נשבר ואנחנו נמלטנו: עזרנו בשם ה' עשה שמים וארץ:

[context] And may we see him, eye to eye,
when he returneth to his habitation, as it is written, For they shall see eye to eye, when the Lord returneth unto Zion. And it is said, And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together ; for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it. May the Father of mercy have mercy upon a people that have been borne by him. May he remember the covenant with the patriarchs, deliver our souls from evil hours, check the evil inclination in them that have been carried by him, grant us of his grace an everlasting deliverance, and in the attribute of his goodness fulfil our desires by salvation and mercy.
And this is the Law which Moses set before the children of Israel, according to the commandment of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
Let them praise the name of the Lord ; for his name alone is exalted : His majesty is above the earth and heaven ; and he hath lifted up a horn for his people, to the praise of all his loving ones, even of the children of Israel, the people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.
And when it rested, he said, Return, O Lord, unto the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, unto thy resting place; thou, and the ark of thy strength. Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy loving ones shout for joy. For the sake of David thy servant, turn not away the face of thine anointed. For I give you good doctrine ; forsake ye not my Law. It is a tree of life to them that grasp it, and of them that uphold it every one is rendered happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Turn thou us unto thee, O Lord, and we shall return : renew our days as of old.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. The Lord answer thee in the day of trouble ; the name of the God of Jacob set thee up on high ; send thee help from the sanctuary, and uphold thee out of Zion ; remember all thy offerings, and accept thy burnt sacrifice (Selah): grant thee thy heart's desire, and fulfil all thy purpose. We will exult in thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners : the Lord fulfil all thy petitions. Now know I that the Lord saveth his anointed ; he will answer him from his holy heaven with the mighty saving acts of his right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses : but we will make mention of the name of the Lord our God. They are bowed down and fallen : but we are risen and stand upright. Save, Lord : may the King answer us on the day when we call.
And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the Lord. And as for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the Lord : my spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever. But thou art holy, O thou that dwellest amid the praises of Israel. And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts : the whole earth is full of his glory. And they receive sanction the one from the other, and say Holy in the highest heavens, the place of his divine abode; holy upon earth, the work of his might ; holy for ever and to all eternity is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of the radiance of his glory. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing (saying), Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing, of those who uttered praises, and said, Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the region of his divine abode. The Lord shall reign for ever and ever. The kingdom of the Lord endureth for ever and to all eternity. O Lord, the God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Israel, our fathers, keep this for ever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of thy people, and direct their heart unto thee. And he, being merciful, forgiveth iniquity and destroyeth not : yea, many a time he turneth his anger away, and doth not stir up all his wrath. For thou, O Lord, art good and forgiving, and abounding in lovingkindness to all them that call upon thee. Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy Law is truth. Thou wilt show truth to Jacob and lovingkindness to Abraham, according as thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day ; if one burdeneth us, God is our salvation. (Selah.) The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. (Selah.) O Lord of hosts, happy is the man who trusteth in thee. Save, Lord : may the King answer us on the day when we call. Blessed is our God, who hath created us for his glory, and hath separated us from them that go astray, and hath given us the Law of truth and planted everlasting life in our midst. May he open our heart unto his Law, and place his love and fear within our hearts, that we may do his will and serve him with a perfect heart, that we may not labour in vain, nor bring forth for confusion. May it be thy will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we may keep thy statutes in this world, and be worthy to live to witness and inherit happiness and blessing in the days of the Messiah and in the life of the world to come. To the end that my glory may sing praise unto thee, and not be silent : O Lord my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever. Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose trust the Lord is. Trust ye in the Lord forever; for in Jah the Lord is an everlasting rock. And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee ; for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, Lord. It pleased the Lord, for his righteousness' sake, to magnify the Law and to make it honourable.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 8:10] O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! [Ps. 31:25] Be strong, and let your heart take courage, All ye that wait for the LORD.
And now, I pray thee, let the power of the Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken. Remember, O Lord, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses ; for they have been ever of old.
Reader.— Magnified and sanctified be his great name in the world which he hath created according to his will. May he establish his kingdom during your life and during your days, and during the life of all the house of Israel, even speedily and at a near time, and say ye, Amen. Cong, and Reader.— Let his great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Reader.— Blessed, praised and glorified, exalted, extolled and honoured, magnified and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be he ; though he be high above all the blessings and hymns, praises and consolations, which are uttered in the world ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— Accept our prayer in mercy and in favour. Reader.— May the prayers and supplications of all Israel be accepted by their Father who is in heaven ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— Let the name of the Lord be blessed from this time forth and for evermore. Reader. — May there be abundant peace from heaven, and life for us and for all Israel ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Reader.— He who maketh peace in his high places, may he make peace for us and for all Israel ; and say ye, Amen.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 86] A Prayer of David. Incline Thine ear, O LORD, and answer me; For I am poor and needy. Keep my soul, for I am godly; O Thou my God, save Thy servant that trusteth in Thee. Be gracious unto me, O Lord; For unto Thee do I cry all the day. Rejoice the soul of Thy servant; For unto Thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul. For Thou, Lord, art good, and ready to pardon, And plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon Thee. Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer; And attend unto the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I call upon Thee; For Thou wilt answer me. There is none like unto Thee among the gods, O Lord, And there are no works like Thine. All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and prostrate themselves before Thee, O Lord; And they shall glorify Thy name. For Thou art great, and doest wondrous things; Thou art God alone. Teach me, O LORD, Thy way, that I may walk in Thy truth; Make one my heart to fear Thy name. I will thank Thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart; And I will glorify Thy name for evermore. For great is Thy mercy toward me; And Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest nether-world. O God, the proud are risen up against me, And the company of violent men have sought after my soul, And have not set Thee before them. But Thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion and gracious, Slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy and truth. O turn unto me, and be gracious unto me; Give Thy strength unto Thy servant, And save the son of Thy handmaid. Work in my behalf a sign for good; That they that hate me may see it, and be put to shame, Because Thou, LORD, hast helped me, and comforted me.
[JPS 1917, Isa. 2:5; Mic. 4:5; 1 Kgs 8:57-60] O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk In the light of the LORD. For let all the peoples walk each one in the name of its god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever. The LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us, nor forsake us; that He may incline our hearts unto Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His ordinances, which He commanded our fathers. And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the LORD, be nigh unto the LORD our God day and night, that He maintain the cause of His servant, and the cause of His people Israel, as every day shall require; that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD, He is God; there is none else.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 124] A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say; 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us, When men rose up against us, Then they had swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us; Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul; Then the proud waters Had gone over our soul.' Blessed be the LORD, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; The snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, Who made heaven and earth.

# Morning Prayer
<note>original: "Tefillat Shacharit"</note>

<note size="small" type="decorative">A decorative printer's ornament is positioned at the top of the page.</note>

Beside them, upon His return to the dwelling, it is written: "For they shall see eye to eye when the Lord returns to Zion." <note>Isaiah 52:8</note> And it says: "And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." <note>Isaiah 40:5</note> The Father of Mercy, He shall comfort the burdened people and remember the covenant of the patriarchs <note>literally "the mighty ones"</note>, and deliver our souls from the evil hours, and rebuke the evil inclination from those who are borne up, and favor us with eternal survival. May He fulfill our requests with the measure of goodness, salvation, and mercy.

<note size="small" type="decorative">Decorative ornament</note>

The seat of the Prophets, the book of awe... etc.
And this is the Torah which Moses set before the children of Israel, by the mouth of the Lord, by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted.
His majesty is over earth and heaven. He has lifted up a horn for His people, a praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people close to Him. Hallelujah!

And he says "In the name" standing for the generation, and it is written... <note>The text here contains abbreviated liturgical instructions for the reader</note>.

And with confidence he said: "Return, O Lord, to the ten thousand thousands of Israel." "Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength." "Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy." "For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed." "For I have given you a good teaching; do not forsake My Torah." "It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it, and those who support it are happy." "Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace." "Turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old." "Happy are they..."

For the conductor, a psalm of David. May the Lord answer you in the day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high. May He send your help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifices. Selah. May He grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in Your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your requests. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heavens with the mighty acts of the salvation of His right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have placed in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, nor from the mouth of your seed's seed, says the Lord, from now and forever.

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another and said: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory." And they receive sanction from one another and say: "Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His Presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His power; holy forever and for all eternity." The Lord of Hosts fills all the earth with the radiance of His glory. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rushing: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place." <note>Aramaic translation follows the Hebrew verses of the Kedushah</note>. Then a wind lifted me up and I heard behind me a sound of great movement of those who praise and say: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His Presence." The Lord shall reign forever and ever. The Lord, His kingship stands forever and for all eternity. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever as the intent of the thoughts of the heart of Your people, and direct their heart to You. And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; frequently He turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abounding in kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You have sworn to our fathers from days of old. Blessed be the Lord, day by day He bears our burden, the God of our salvation. Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah. Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is He, our God, who created us for His glory, and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us a Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our heart through His Torah, and place in our heart love and awe of Him, to do His will and serve Him with a perfect heart, so that we do not labor in vain nor give birth for terror. May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing in the years of the Messianic age and the life of the World to Come. So that my soul <note>literally "glory"</note> may sing to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his trust. Trust in the Lord forever, for in God the Lord is an everlasting Rock. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. The Lord desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
Be strong and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the Lord.

And now, may the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies and Your kindnesses, for they have been from of old.

Exalted and hallowed be His great name. In the world which He created according to His will, may He establish His kingdom, and may His salvation flourish, and may He bring near the <note>alternate version: end of</note> His Messiah. In your lifetime and in your days, and in the life of all the House of Israel, speedily and in a near time; and say, Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised, glorified and exalted, extolled and honored, adored and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Beyond <note>abbreviation for: "above and beyond"</note> all the blessings and hymns, praises and consolations that are uttered in the world; and say, Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and favor our prayer. May the prayer and supplication of all the House of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven; and say, Amen. May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be abundant peace from heaven, and life for us and for all Israel; and say, Amen. My help is from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His heights, may He make peace for us and for all Israel; and say, Amen.

A prayer of David. Incline Your ear, O Lord, and answer me, for I am poor and needy. Guard my soul, for I am pious; save Your servant who trusts in You, You are my God. Be gracious to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abounding in kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and listen to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my distress I call upon You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, O Lord, and shall honor Your name. For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God. Teach me, O Lord, Your way; I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your name. I will thank You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever. For Your kindness toward me is great, and You have delivered my soul from the lowest depths. O God, arrogant men have risen against me, and a company of ruthless men have sought my life, and have not set You before them. But You, O Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Work with me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because You, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

O House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of his god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever. May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers; may He not leave us nor forsake us. To incline our heart to Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His ordinances which He commanded our fathers. And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, that He may maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is no other.

A song of ascents, of David. If the Lord had not been for us—let Israel now say. If the Lord had not been for us when man rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us alive when their anger was kindled against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have passed over our soul. Then the treacherous waters would have passed over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

We will sing for joy in Thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all thy petitions. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heavens with the saving strength of His right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon thee, and My words which I have placed in thy mouth, shall not depart from thy mouth, nor from the mouth of thy seed, nor from the mouth of thy seed’s seed, says the Lord, from henceforth and forever.

And Thou art holy, inhabiting the praises of Israel. And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory. And they receive <note>clarification: the word</note> one from another, and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His Presence <note>term>Shekhinah</note>; Holy upon the earth, the work of His power; Holy forever and to all eternity. The Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of the radiance of His glory. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me a sound of a great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place. And a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great movement of those who praise and say: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His Presence. The Lord shall reign forever and ever. The Lord, His kingdom stands forever and to all eternity. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of the heart of Thy people, and direct their heart toward Thee. And He, being merciful, forgiveth iniquity and destroyeth not; yea, many a time He turneth His anger away and stirreth not up all His wrath. For Thou, O Lord, art good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon Thee. Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy Torah is truth. Thou wilt show truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as Thou hast sworn to our fathers from the days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day, who bears our burden; God is our salvation. Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah. O Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in Thee. O Lord, save; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed be He, our God, who created us for His glory, and separated us from those who err, and gave us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our heart through His Torah, and place in our heart His love and fear, to do His will and to serve Him with a perfect heart, so that we may not labor in vain, nor bring forth for terror. May it be Thy will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we may keep Thy statutes in this world, and merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing for the years of the Messianic age and for the life of the world to come. To the end that my glory may sing praise to Thee and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will give thanks to Thee forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his trust. Trust in the Lord forever and ever, for in Yah <note>term>Yah</note> the Lord is an everlasting Rock. And those who know Thy name will trust in Thee, for Thou hast not forsaken those who seek Thee, O Lord. The Lord was pleased for His righteousness' sake to magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Thy name in all the earth.
Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the Lord.

And now, I pray Thee, let the power of the Lord be great, according as Thou hast spoken, saying: Remember Thy mercies, O Lord, and Thy kindnesses, for they have been from of old.

Magnified and sanctified be His great name <note>term>Kaddish</note> <gloss>Sanctification prayer</gloss> in the world which He created according to His will. May He establish His kingdom, and cause His salvation to spring forth, and hasten the coming of <note>alternative: or "draw near the end of"</note> His Messiah. In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and in a near time; and say, Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised and glorified and exalted and extolled and honored and uplifted and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Above <note>original: "לעילא"</note> (from all and above all) all blessings and songs, praises and consolations that are uttered in the world; and say, Amen. Accept, accept with mercy and with favor our prayer. May the prayer and the supplication of all the house of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven; and say, Amen. Receive, may the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be great peace from heaven, and life for us and for all Israel; and say, Amen. My help is from the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His high places, may He make peace for us and for all Israel; and say, Amen.

A prayer of David. Incline Thine ear, O Lord, answer me, for I am poor and needy. Preserve my soul, for I am pious; O Thou my God, save Thy servant who trusts in Thee. Be gracious unto me, O Lord, for unto Thee do I cry all day long. Rejoice the soul of Thy servant, for unto Thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul. For Thou, O Lord, art good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon Thee. Give ear, O Lord, unto my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I will call upon Thee, for Thou wilt answer me. There is none like Thee among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Thine. All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and bow down before Thee, O Lord, and they shall glorify Thy name. For Thou art great and doest wonders; Thou art God alone. Teach me, O Lord, Thy way; I will walk in Thy truth; unite my heart to fear Thy name. I will thank Thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify Thy name forever. For Thy kindness is great toward me, and Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest nether-world. O God, the proud have risen up against me, and a congregation of violent men have sought my soul, and have not set Thee before them. But Thou, O Lord, art a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and truth. Turn unto me and be gracious unto me; give Thy strength unto Thy servant, and save the son of Thy handmaid. Work for me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because Thou, O Lord, hast helped me and comforted me.

O house of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each one in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us nor forsake us. To incline our heart toward Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His judgments, which He commanded our fathers. And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the Lord, be near unto the Lord our God day and night, that He maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as every day shall require. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is none else.

A Song of Ascents, of David. If the Lord had not been for us, let Israel now say: If the Lord had not been for us when man rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul. Then the treacherous waters would have gone over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped like a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

May He send your help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifice forever. [context] This great Abasside
is extremely kind towards the Jews, many of his officers being of that nation; he understands all languages, is well versed in the mosaic law and reads and writes the hebrew language.
He enjoys nothing, but what he earns by the labour of his own hands and therefore manufactures coverlets which he stamps with his seal and which his officers sell in the public market; these articles are purchased by the nobles of the land and from their produce his necessaries are provided.
The Khalif is an excellent man, trustworthy and kind-hearted towards every one, but generally invisible to the mahomedans. The pilgrims, which come hither from distant countries on their way to Mekha in Yemen, desire to be presented to him and thus address him from the palace: 'Our Lord, light of the mahomedans and splendor of our religion, show us the brightness of thy countenance', but he heeds not their words. His servants and officers then approach and pray: 'O Lord, manifest thy peace to those men, who come from distant lands and desire shelter in the shadow of thy glory' and after such petition he rises and puts one corner of his garment out of the window,
[context] which is eagerly kissed by the pilgrims.

<meta>Single column of main Zohar text from Parashat Terumah. This page discusses the mystical significance of the Cherubim (Keruvim), the balance between Mercy (Chesed) and Judgment (Din), and includes the famous Kabbalistic parable of the villager and the wheat (Chittin), illustrating how divine essence is hidden within layers of manifestation.</meta>
<vocab>דינא, חסד, רחמי, כרובים, קודשא בריך הוא, ספרא, היכלא, חטין, מתקלא</vocab>

## Main Text (Zohar)

דזיוו — כלהו לוקמוהי. **רבי אלעזר** סח ליצחק מנו דיכא קטיא כפף דקה יצחק דיכא קטיא חמיל לחולקיה ח"ו רגז ולא הוה כחולקיה והא יצחק מנו חסד כפחא וק' כי כלהו דינא מנו רחמי כפחא ורחמי מליכא. חכרה ירית לחסדא דחסד כפף ויצחק כדינא מנו חסד יצחק כפף ברחמי מנו דינא קשיא ובך הוה לעילא דא מן דא ונפק ליה מן דא עד דאשתמודע כלא דכהא חד ומהד תליין כלהו וכלא לאשתכח חד צריך שמיא לעלם ולעלמי עלמין. **רבי אלעזר** אסתמודע דלית סרטין דל לה כד חזינן לה כדא וחד חמיד בתרווייהו לסכללא כלא כגון יעקב והיינו דכתיב:
> מברח מן הקצה אל הקצה <note>שמות כו:כח</note>

תוכח כלי דאי לא תקרי אלא מסטרא דילן ומסטרא דילן אשתמודע כלא כהו יכילא כלא בחד מתקלא סלקא לא שכי ולא ישתני כמה דכתיב:
> אני יי' לא שניתי <note>מלאכי ג:ו</note>

**רבי יהודה** כלהון כוסיפין נהירין מהד ומהד תליין וכונניו היכהו חד כלא ולא לאתפרשא ומאן דפריש לון בחיליה אתפרש מן חיי עלמין. **רבי יצחק** כתיב:
> ונתתי נערים שריהם ותעלולים ימשלו בם <note>ישעיהו ג:ד</note>

היינו דכתיב ועזים פנים כרובים ודא וכתיב יושב הכרובים וכתיב וירכב על כרוב ויעף. יושב הכרובים כד שריא לאתיישבא בסיועותא כתיב יושב הכרובים (דא כד אשתכח בשלימותא) וירכב על כרוב חד דלא אתיישבא מלכא בכרסייה. יושב הכרובים תרי. לדייפי ווי לעלמא כד חד כרוב להדר אנפי מתבריא דהא כתיב:
> ופניהם איש אל אחיו <note>שמות כה:כ</note>

כד הוו שלמא בעלמא. **רבי יצחק** קל תנינן ערוה לבין ונערות חמך לא תגלה ווי למאן דגלי עריתהון כגוונא דא כתיב ביעקב מברח מן הקצה אל הקצה. וכהא חולקהון דישראל לקודשא בריך הוא אשתכח בתכשיטייהו כגוונא דלעילא דכתיב:
> ישראל אשר בך אתפאר <note>ישעיהו מט:ג</note>

תא חזי **רבי יצחק** ביומי קדמוהי הוי כד חד אמר לחבריה חומא לי מנא חדא וטול מנה כסף. השתא אמר בר נש לחבריה טול מנה כסף ואחמתלא בחוריתא ולית מין דיטעם ולית מאן דירכון חולכיה בר חיכון זעירין קליטין עלינין לקודשא בריך הוא אשתכח כהו דכתיב:
> ועמך כלם צדיקים לעולם ירשו ארץ נצר מטעי מעשה ידי להתפאר <note>ישעיהו ס:כא</note>

ווי דיתמליס ומתקיימא כסף. **רבי יצחק** אמר ווי כי נמולים קא חמינא כל חינון דמתתאלן מקטרי קיימין עלאין חקרון ווי דיתמליס וכל חיכון לנתתא תליין חחיכון ווי. חלונותא פתח בנו פתח ומתחלדן ומתתקנין מקוטרא לסדרא דקחיס עלייהו. וכספרא דכביעותא תוכח ווי לעילא ווי לתתא וכלהו במתקלא חד סלקין. מאן דביעותא דספרא **אמר רבי חזקיה** פרקין חינון דכולהן בהיכל רב ומליין כל ארעא. **רבי יהודה** חי כולהן הכי מכהו עדיפי. **אמר רבי** קבי הוי למאן דעט וכפף ולמאן דלא עלה וכפף להו הכי.

---

### The Parable of the Wheat

מתלא לבר נש דהוה דיירין ביני דברין ולא ידע בדיורי מתא. וזרע חטין ואכל חטין כגופייהו. יומא חד עאל למתא לקריבוסו כקמא טבא. אמר מהא בר נש דכא למה. אמרו כקמא הוא למיכל. אכל וטעם אחלא למכיה. **אמר רבי** מרוממא דא עביד דא. אמרו חטין. לבתר דקריבוסו גרונין דליסין במתחא. טעם מכיהו אמר וחלינומתא התנבידי. אמרו חטין. לבתר דקריבונו טריקי מלכין דליסין בדובשא ומשחא. אמר וחלויין חמת עבידו. אמרו חטין. אמר ודאי חכא מחרי לכל חלין דהכא חכיל עקרא דכל חלין דהיכו חטי. ובגין ההוא...

Said R. Eleazar: ‘It would seem that Jacob emanated from the region of severe Judgement, for Isaac laid hold on this attribute as his portion.’ Said R. Simeon to him: ‘But was this the only grade? Isaac emanated from Grace, surely, and so did all the Fathers. In fact, Judgement proceeds from Mercy, and Mercy from Judgement. Abraham inherited Mercy, and Isaac proceeded therefrom, but with the aura of Judgement about him; and Jacob in turn issued in Mercy from the midst of Judgement. So one quality emanates from another, each imbibes from each, and finally it is made manifest that all are one, and all depend on One, and the One is all in all. Blessed be His Name for ever and ever.’
Said R. Eleazar: ‘It is evident that there can be no perfection except the one aspect be joined to the other and a third hold them together to harmonize and complete them, like Jacob in relation to Abraham and Isaac. That is why it is written: “And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall be fastening from one end to the other.”
We have been taught that all this differentiation of the Divine Personality is from our side and relative to our knowledge, and that, above, all is one, all is set in one balance, unvarying and eternal, as it is written: “I the Lord change not” (Mal. 3, 6).’ Said R. Judah: ‘All the heavenly lights are illumined from one and depend on one, and all the lights there form only one Light, and desire never to be separated, and he who does separate them in his mind is as though he separated himself from life eternal.’
Said R. Isaac: ‘It is written, “And I will give youths to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them” (Isa. 3, 4). This is an allusion to the words, “And thou shalt make two cherubims of gold” (Ex. 25, 18). It is also written: “The ark of the Lord which dwelleth between the cherubims” (I Sam. 4, 4); and again it is written, “And he rode upon a cherub” (2 Sam. 22, 11). When He dwells in completeness, He “dwelleth between cherubims”, but when the King is not established on His Throne, He “rides” on “one” cherub.
Said R. Jose: ‘Woe unto the world when one cherub turns away his face from the other, for it is written, “And their faces shall look one to another” (Ex. 25, 20); only then is there harmony in the world.’ Said R. Isaac: ‘We have been taught that the words, “The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover” (Lev. 18, 7) have an esoteric reference to supermundane relationships in addition to their obvious significance. Woe to him who “uncovers their nakedness” (by probing too deeply into the hidden mysteries of the inner aspects of the Divine Essence and the relationship of one to another). Similarly, it is written in regard to Jacob: “fastening from one end to the other”. Happy is the lot of Israel, by whose praises the Holy One, blessed be He, is glorified even as He is glorified above: “Israel in whom I am glorified” (Isa. 49, 3).’
We have been taught that R. Isaac once said: ‘In bygone times a person used to say to his neighbour, “Speak to me on a certain portion of the Torah and I will pay thee for it”; but in our days, even if one person says to another, “Study the Torah and I will reward thee with money for so doing”, no one inclines his ears to listen, and none desires knowledge except those few saints of the Highest in whom the Holy One is glorified, and concerning whom it is written, “And thy people shall be all righteous, they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified” (Ibid. 60, 21).’
THE HOOKS OF THE PILLARS AND THEIR FILLETS SHALL BE OF SILVER. Said R. Isaac: ‘I presume that the “hooks of the pillars” symbolize all those who are attached to the supernal unifying pillars, and that all those who are below depend on them. What is the significance of the word vavim (hooks; also the letter vau, the numerical value of which is six)? Six within six (vv), all united and nourished by the Spine which is set over them. And we have learnt in the Book of the Hidden Mystery (Sifra di-zenintha) this dictum: “Hooks above, hooks below (six above, six below), all comprehended in one meaning and one name, having one and the same significance.”
Now, what is this “Book of the Hidden Mystery”?’ Said R. Simeon: ‘It contains five sections which are to be found in the midst of a great Hall, and whose wisdom fills the whole earth.’ Said R. Judah: ‘If this book of wisdom is enclosed in that Hall, it is of more worth than any other tome.’ ‘Verily,’ returned R. Simeon, ‘it is so, for one who is used to passing in and out of the courts of wisdom, but not to one who rarely or never enters into that Hall.
Once there was a man who dwelt among the mountains and was a complete stranger to the ways of townsfolk. He sowed wheat, but knew no better than to consume it in its natural condition. One day he went down into a city, and there a loaf of good bread was placed before him. He asked what it was, and was informed that it was bread and was meant to eat. He ate it and liked it. “What is it made of?” he said. They told him “Wheat”. Later, he was given fine cake kneaded in oil. He tasted it, and again asked: “And this, of what is it made?” The same reply was made as before: “Of wheat”. Finally, he was treated to some royal confectionery, flavoured with oil and honey. Once more he asked his question, and obtained the same reply. Then he said: “In sooth, I have all these at my command, because I eat the essential constituent of all, namely wheat.”
[context] Thus, through his untutored taste he remained a stranger to all these delicious flavours, and their enjoyment was lost to him.

The radiance of all things—all of them were established by the teachers. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is the <term>deika katya</term> <gloss>broken-hearted or humble one</gloss>? Isaac bowed his head. Isaac was humble regarding his portion, Heaven forbid he should be angry, for his portion was not like the others. And behold, Isaac represents <term>Gevurah</term> <gloss>Strength/Judgment</gloss>, yet he is called <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> when he is bowed down. For all Judgment is sweetened by Mercy, and Mercy is from the King. Wisdom inherits Mercy, for Mercy bows, and Isaac as Judgment is included in Mercy. Isaac bows before Mercy, for out of it comes harsh Judgment. And so it is above, this one from that one, and this one emerging from that one, until everything is known as one. They all depend on one another, and for all to be found as one, Heaven is needed forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no divisions when we see it as one, and one desire is in both of them to complete the whole, such as Jacob. This is what is written: 
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves the whole; for if you do not read it but from our side and from the other side, all is known. All things can rise in a single balance, not changing and not shifting, as it is written:
> I am the Lord, I change not <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: All these lights shine from one another and depend on one another. They are established as one whole, not to be separated. Whoever separates them by his own power is separated from the life of the worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** noted what is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This refers to the "brazen-faced" <note>impudent</note> Cherubim. It is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is also written, "And He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when the Divine Presence dwells in stability and support <note>this is when perfection is found</note>. "He rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King is not settled on His throne. "Sits upon the Cherubim" refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from the other, for it is written:
> and their faces shall look one to another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This occurs when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "The nakedness of a daughter-in-law or a daughter thou shalt not uncover." Woe to him who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner it is written of Jacob, "passing through from end to end." Thus is the portion of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He; they are found in their adornments just as it is above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In former days, when one said to his fellow, "Show me one vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to his fellow, "Take money and show me a different thing," and there is no one to taste and no one to incline his portion, except for those few who are gathered and high unto the Holy One, blessed be He. As it is written:
> Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the money is fulfilled and sustained. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, all those who are crowned by the upper knots, searching. Woe that it is fulfilled, for all those below depend on those above, woe. A window opens within a window, and they are renewed and prepared from the smoke for the order that rests upon them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>Sifra Detzniuta</note>, it is proven: Woe above, woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. What is the fear of the Book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These sections are all in the Great Palace and fill all the earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are thus, and even better than this. **The Rabbi said**: Woe to him who turns away and bows, and to him who did not ascend and bow to them in this way.

---

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived among the fields and did not know the ways of the city dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat as it was <note>raw grains</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good fine bread. He asked, "What is this for?" They said, "It is bread to eat." He ate it and found it very pleasant to his taste. **The Rabbi said**: "This is made from what?" They said, "From wheat." Later they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said, "And from what are these made?" They said, "From wheat." Later they brought him royal pastries made with honey and oil. He said, "And what are these delicacies made of?" They said, "From wheat." He said, "Truly, I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat." And because of that...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical unity of the Divine attributes, emphasizing that Judgment and Mercy must be balanced. It uses the Cherubim as symbols of cosmic harmony and concludes with a famous parable illustrating how the simple essence of Torah is hidden within complex layers of wisdom.</summary>
<keywords>Cherubim, Jacob, Isaac, Balance, Mercy, Judgment, Parable of Wheat, Sifra Detzniuta, Unity</keywords>

Of the radiance—they have all established it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is the one whose spirit is humbled? Isaac bent down, for Isaac was humbled and took pity on his portion. God forbid that he should be angry, for his portion was not like theirs. And behold, Isaac is from the side of <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> when he is humbled, and yet we see that all his attributes are <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. He is from the side of <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Compassion</gloss> when he is humbled, and compassion belongs to the King. Wisdom inherits Mercy, for Mercy bows down. And Isaac, though acting in Judgment, is sourced in Mercy. Isaac bowed before Compassion, though he is the source of harsh Judgment. And so it was above, one from the other, and it emerged from this one until that one, until everything was recognized as one. All things are suspended from one another, and for everything to be found as one, the heavens are needed forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no paths except for her, when we see her as one. And one desires both of them to complete the whole, just as Jacob did, as it is written:
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves the whole. For if you do not read it except from our side and from the other side, the whole is recognized. Everything is weighed in a single <term>matkala</term> <gloss>balance or scale</gloss>; it does not waver and does not change, as it is written:
> I the Lord do not change <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: All the hidden lights shine from one another and are suspended from one another. Their foundation is one, a single whole, never to be separated. Whoever separates them through his own power is separated from the life of the worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** noted it is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is as it is written: the bold-faced ones are the <term>Keruvim</term> <gloss>Cherubim</gloss>. And it is written: "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written: "And he rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when He dwells in a settled state of support <note>when found in perfection</note>. "And he rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King is not settled upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note> refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns his face away from the other, for it is written:
> and their faces shall look one to another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This occurs when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "Do not uncover the nakedness of a daughter-in-law or a young woman." Woe to the one who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner it is written of Jacob: "passing through from end to end." And thus is the portion of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He; they are found in their adornments in the likeness of the upper world, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In former days, when one said to his fellow, "Show me one vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to his fellow, "Take money and show me a vision," and there is none who can taste it and none who can bow his portion, except for those few refined ones who are high up. For the Holy One, blessed be He, is found among them, as it is written:
> And your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the silver is depleted and remains. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see that those who are circumcised and tied to the upper knots are being investigated. I replied, "And could I be ignorant of Abu Zayd? He is one whose wounds are vast, and every judge has heard stories and news of him." At that moment, I shaved my head and regained my senses, but only after the time had passed. I realized then that every bit of his malice was a trap and a planned artifice. What I encountered made me lower my gaze in shame, and I swore never to deal with the likes of those two as long as I lived. Then I began to sigh over the loss of my best deal and my disgrace among my companions.

When the judge saw what I was going through, he realized my distress was that of a free man. He said, "O man, whatever money you lost was not truly gone if it served as a sermon to you, and he who woke you up committed no crime against you. Take heed of what has come to you, and let what befell your companions be a reminder of what struck you. Keep this memory so that your lost coins may serve as a reminder, for he who is afflicted and remains patient, and then sees the lesson clearly and takes it to heart, will find renewal." So I bid him farewell, walking with a gait of shame and sorrow, dragging the hem of loss and fraud. I intended to confront Abu Zayd with the news and speak to him frankly.

[context] Dimna instantly replied, that there were several impediments to the good administration of public affairs which might be mentioned; for instance, favouritism, which founded generally on caprice or some worse motive, gives the reins of government into feeble if not polluted hands, to the proscription of those faithful counsellors of a nation, who have courage to refuse becoming the tools of the passions of the prince : another evil of the body politic is that animosity of parties, which is continually keeping up a petty warfare in the state :
a third source of mischief is a profligacy of manners, when respect for decency in the prince and the higher circles has fled before the fascinating and authorized display of female attractions, and the severity of business is lulled to sleep in the lap of luxurious amusement and excess : the prevalence of these disorders gives rise to and nurtures those unfeeling and inhuman passions, by which calumny is engendered, and the tongue sends forth its venom to taint the bliss and satisfaction of conspicuous worth ; or the arm is lifted up to acts of violence and oppression; or dangers arise from the practice of severity where gentleness was called for ; or of indulgence when severity would have been a virtue ; or, lastly, the hand of time becomes visible in the age and infirmities of the sovereign, or in his exposure to the plagues of famine or war; and the conduct of the lion, continued he, in the preference which he has shewn to the bull, will prove in all probability a source of some of the dangers which I have enumerated. Granted, replied Kalila, but how will you contrive to get the better of the bull, considering the reputation which he enjoys. You seem to draw your conclusions, answered Dimna, from the apparent weakness of my person, compared with that of the bull, without reflecting that bodily force is not always the criterion of success; on the contrary, contrivance and skill have been often known to succeed where the greatest exertion of strength would have failed, as was exemplified by the manner in which a crow destroyed a serpent, as related in the following story. A crow had made her nest in a tree upon a mountain, at no great distance from which was the hole of a serpent ; and the serpent, as soon as the crow had hatched her young, came and took them away, and ate them. This very much distressed the crow, who went and made her complaint to a jackal, who was her friend, and asked his opinion of what she proposed to do, which was, when the serpent was asleep, to put out his eyes, and get rid of her enemy. The jackal did not at all approve of this plan, but advised the crow to think of some other method, which would be attended with less danger; because if she proceeded as she had mentioned, she might possibly experience the fate of the swan, who perished in his attempt to kill a crab.

[context] The moon too,
the companion of the sun, has many names, e.g. Soma, because she is lucky, and everything lucky is called somagraha, whilst all that is unlucky is called papagraha. Further, Nisesa, i.e. lord of the night, Nakshatranatha, i.e. lord of the lunar stations, Dvijesvara, i.e. lord of the Brahmins, Sitamsu, i.e. having a cold ray, because the moon's globe is watery, which is a blessing to the earth. When the solar ray meets the moon, the ray becomes as cool as the moon herself, then, being reflected, it illuminates the darkness, makes the night cool and extinguishes any hurtful kind of combustion wrought by the sun. Similarly the moon is also called Candra, which means the left eye of Narayana, as the sun is his right eye.
The following table exhibits the names of the months. Disturbances and differences in lists of these names proceed from the causes which we shall mention (v. p. 228) when speaking of the enumeration of the different earths.

The companion and follower of the Sun <note>referring to the Moon</note> also has many names. Among them is <term>Soma</term> <gloss>the Auspicious</gloss> because it is fortunate. Fortunate stars are called <term>Saumya-graha</term> <gloss>benign planets</gloss> and the unfortunate ones are <term>Papa-graha</term> <gloss>malevolent planets</gloss>. Other names include <term>Nishisha</term> <gloss>Lord of the Night</gloss>, <term>Nakshatranatha</term> <gloss>Lord of the Lunar Mansions</gloss>, <term>Dvijeshvara</term> <gloss>Lord of the Twice-born</gloss>, and <term>Shitanshu</term> <gloss>Cold-rayed</gloss>. This is because its sphere is composed of water, and it contains contentment. When solar rays fall upon it, they become cold like its own nature; the light reflects to illuminate the darkness, cooling the night and extinguishing the burning damage caused by the Sun. For this reason, it is also called <term>Chandra</term> <gloss>The Shiner</gloss>. It is the left eye of <term>Narayana</term> <gloss>the Supreme Being in Hinduism</gloss>, just as the Sun is his right eye. In this table, I have deposited the names of the Suns of the months. The variations found in them arise from the same causes previously mentioned regarding the measurements of the Earths.
