If they lack the heart of a beast, even those with the physical form of a beast will be treated with affection. Traditions tell of creatures with horns, separated teeth, spread claws, those that fly above, and those that crawl below; these are called birds and beasts, yet they do not necessarily lack the heart of a human. Although they may have the heart of a human, they are treated with distance because of their appearance. <margin>These two points are agreeable</margin> <margin>Liezi: Yellow Emperor</margin>

<term>Paoxi</term> <gloss>Fuxi</gloss>, <term>Nuwa</term>, <term>Shennong</term>, and the Lord of Xia <note>Yu the Great</note> had bodies like snakes, faces of humans, heads of oxen, or noses of tigers. These possessed forms that were not human, yet they possessed the virtue of great sages. 

Xia Jie, Yin Zhou, Huan of Lu, and Mu of Chu had appearances and facial features <note>literally "seven orifices"</note> just like other humans, yet they possessed the hearts of birds and beasts. If the common people rely solely on outward appearance to seek the highest wisdom, they will never come close to finding it.

The <term>Yellow Emperor</term> <gloss>Huangdi</gloss> fought the <term>Flame Emperor</term> <gloss>Yandi</gloss> at the wilderness of <term>Banquan</term>. He led bears, grizzly bears, wolves, leopards, <term>pixiu</term> <gloss>fabulous fierce beasts</gloss>, and tigers as his front scouts, while using eagles, harriers, hawks, and kites as his banners. This was a case of using power to command birds and beasts. When <term>Yao</term> commanded <term>Kui</term> to direct the music, they struck and patted the stones, and all the beasts followed in dance. When the <term>Xiaoshao</term> music was played in nine movements, the phoenixes came to present themselves.

<summary>This passage argues that internal virtue and intelligence are independent of physical form, citing ancient sages with animal features and wicked kings with human appearances. It also describes the mythical ability of sovereign rulers like the Yellow Emperor and Yao to command and harmonize with animals.</summary>

If they lack the heart of a beast, even if they have the physical form of a beast, they will be treated with affection because of their appearance. Tradition says that those with horns, segmented teeth, spread claws, those that fly upward or crawl downward, are called birds and beasts; yet they do not necessarily lack a human heart. These possessed forms that were not human, yet they possessed the virtue of great sages. <margin>These two points are agreeable.</margin> Xia Jie, Yin Zhou, Lu Huan, and Chu Mu <note>notorious tyrants and failed rulers of Chinese history</note> were identical to other humans in their appearance and the seven apertures of their heads, yet they possessed the hearts of birds and beasts. If the masses rely solely on a single physical form to seek supreme wisdom, they will never come close to finding it. The <term>Huangdi</term> <gloss>Yellow Emperor</gloss> fought the <term>Yandi</term> <gloss>Flame Emperor</gloss> at the wilderness of Banquan. This is an example of using power to command birds and beasts. Yao commanded Kui <note>a one-legged mythical figure and master of music</note> to direct the music. When the <term>Xiaoshao</term> <gloss>the music of Shun</gloss> was played in nine movements, the phoenixes came to present themselves. <margin>Liezi: Yellow Emperor.</margin>

<note>clarification: If a creature</note> must lack the heart of a beast, then even if it has the heart of a beast, it will be treated with intimacy because of its appearance. It is said that those with horns, split teeth, spread claws, those that fly upwards or crouch and walk are called birds and beasts; yet they do not necessarily lack the heart of a man. Even if they have the heart of a man, they are treated with distance because of their appearance. The <term>Paoxi</term> <gloss>Fuxi</gloss> clan, the <term>Nüwa</term> clan, the <term>Shennong</term> clan, and the <term>Xiahou</term> <gloss>Yu the Great</gloss> clan had bodies of snakes and faces of men, or heads of oxen and noses of tigers. These had the appearance of non-humans but possessed the virtue of great sages. <term>Jie</term> of the <term>Xia</term>, <term>Zhou</term> of the <term>Yin</term>, <term>Huan</term> of <term>Lu</term>, and <term>Mu</term> of <term>Chu</term> had appearances and the seven apertures <note>clarification: the eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth</note> all identical to men, yet they had the hearts of birds and beasts. If the masses rely solely on appearance to seek supreme wisdom, they will never come close to it. The Yellow Emperor <note>original: "黃帝"</note> fought the Flame Emperor <note>original: "炎帝"</note> in the wilds of <term>Banquan</term>. He led bears, grizzly bears, wolves, leopards, <term>pixiu</term> <gloss>mythological fierce beasts</gloss>, and tigers as the vanguard; he used eagles, hawks, falcons, and kites for his banners. This is an example of using power to command birds and beasts. <term>Yao</term> commanded <term>Kui</term> to preside over the music. When they struck the stones and patted the stones <note>clarification: lithophones</note>, the hundred beasts led each other in dance. When the <term>Xiaoshao</term> <gloss>music of Shun</gloss> reached nine movements, the phoenixes came to present themselves.

<summary>The text argues that true virtue and wisdom are not determined by outward appearance, citing sages with beast-like forms and tyrants with human forms, and describes the Yellow Emperor and Yao's command over animals.</summary>
<keywords>Yellow Emperor, Flame Emperor, Banquan, Nüwa, Shennong, Fuxi, virtue vs. appearance, animal allegory, ancient sages</keywords>

अथ खलु मञ्जुश्रीः कुमारभूतो भगवन्तमेतदवोचत्—दुष्करं भगवन् परमदुष्कर-

गोचरः ? यदा च मञ्जुश्रीर्बोधिसत्त्वो महासत्त्वो न राजानं संसेवते, न राजपुत्रान् न राज-

परिव्राजकाजीविकनिर्ग्रन्थान् न काव्यशास्त्रप्रसृतान् सत्त्वान् संसेवते, न भजते न पर्युपास्ते,

<margin>N 181</margin>
लुब्धकान् न मांसिकान् न नटनृत्तकान् न झल्लान् न मल्लान् । अन्यानि परेषां रतिक्रीडा-

प्रतिसंमोदयति । न च पण्डकस्य धर्मं देशयति, न च तेन सार्धं संस्तवं करोति,

भावयमानः । सचेत्पुनर्मातृग्रामस्य धर्मं देशयति, स नान्तशो धर्मसंरागेणापि धर्मं

PEACEFUL LIFE.

Mazgusri, the prince royal, said to the Lord: It is difficult, Lord, most difficult, what these Bodhisattvas Mahasattvas will attempt out of reverence for the Lord. How are these Bodhisattvas MahAsattvas to promulgate this Dharmaparydya at the end of time, at the last period? Whereupon the Lord answered Mazgusri, the prince royal: A Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Mazgusri, he who is to promulgate this Dharmaparydya at the end of time, at the last period, must be firm in four things. In which things? The Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Ma#gusri, must be firm in his conduct and proper sphere if he wishes to teach this Dharmaparyaya. And how, Maggusri, is a Bodhisattva Mahasattva firm in his conduct and proper sphere? When the Bodhisattva Mahdsattva, Ma#gusri, is patient, meek, has reached the stage of meekness ; when he is not rash, nor envious; when, moreover, Mazigusri, he clings to no law whatever and sees the real character of the laws (or things) ; when he is refraining from investigating and discussing these laws, Mazigusri; that is called the conduct of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva. And what is the proper sphere of a Bodhisattva Mahdsattva, Mazgusri ? When the Bodhisattva Mahasattva, Ma#gusri, does not serve, not court, not wait upon kings; does not serve, not court, not wait upon princes; when he does not approach them; when he does not serve, not court, not wait upon persons of another sect, Aarakas, Parivragakas, Agivakas, Nirgranthas, nor persons passionately fond of fine literature; when he does not serve, not court, not wait upon adepts at worldly spells, and votaries of a worldly philosophy, nor keep any intercourse with them ; when he does not go to see KAndalas, jugglers, vendors of pork, poulterers, deer-hunters, butchers, actors and dancers, wrestlers, nor resort to places whither others flock for amusement and sport; when he keeps no intercourse with them unless from time to time to preach the law to them when they come to him, and that freely; when he does not serve, not court, not wait upon monks, nuns, lay devotees, male and female, who are adherents of the vehicle of disciples, nor keep intercourse with them ; when he does not come in contact with them at the place of promenade or in the monastery, unless from time to time to preach the law to them when they come to him, and even that freely. This, Mazgusri, is the proper sphere of a Bodhisattva Mahdasattva.

Again, Maagusri, the Bodhisattva Mahdasattva does not take hold of some favourable opportunity or another to preach the law to females every now and anon, nor is he desirous of repeatedly seeing females ; nor does he think it proper to visit families and then too often address a girl, virgin, or young wife, nor does he greet them too fondly in return. He does not preach the law to a hermaphrodite, keeps no intercourse with such a person, nor greets too friendly in return. He does not enter a house alone in order to receive alms, unless having the Tathagata in his thoughts. And when he happens to preach the law to females, he does not do so by passionate attachment to the law, far less by passionate attachment to a woman. When he is preaching, he does not display his row of teeth, let alone a quick emotion on his physiognomy. He addresses no novice, male or female, no nun, no monk, no young boy, no young girl, nor enters upon a conversation with them; he shows no great readiness in answering their address, nor cares to give too frequent answers. This, Ma#gusri, is called the first proper sphere of a Bodhisattva Mahasattva.

->13. The Chapter on the Pleasant Abode<-

<margin>K 275</margin>
N 180
W 235
Then, the youth <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss> spoke to the Blessed One: Lord, it is difficult, extremely difficult, what these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings dedicated to awakening</gloss> and <term>Mahasattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> have undertaken out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, Lord, should this <term>Dharma-paryaya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> be proclaimed by these Bodhisattvas and Mahasattvas in the later age, in the final time?

When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said to the youth Manjushri: A Bodhisattva and Mahasattva who is established in four qualities, Manjushri, should proclaim this discourse of the teaching in the later age, in the final time. Which four? Here, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva who is established in proper conduct and a proper sphere of activity should proclaim this discourse of the teaching in the later age, in the final time. 

And how, Manjushri, does a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva become established in proper conduct and a proper sphere of activity? When a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva is patient, self-controlled, has reached the level of the disciplined, is not terrified or agitated in mind, and is not critical of others; and when a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva does not engage in any <term>dharma</term> <gloss>phenomenon or practice</gloss> but observes the true nature of things as they are. That which is non-apprehension and non-conceptualization among these things, Manjushri, is called the conduct of a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva. 

And what, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity of a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva? 
<margin>K 276</margin>
W 236
When a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva does not associate with kings, does not associate with princes, royal ministers, or royal officers; does not resort to, serve, or approach them. He does not associate with, resort to, or serve those of other sects such as the wanderers, the mendicants, the <term>Ajivikas</term> <gloss>a sect of fatalist ascetics</gloss>, or the <term>Nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jains</gloss>; nor those devoted to worldly poetry and treatises. He does not associate with, resort to, or serve those who maintain the worldly <term>Lokayata</term> <gloss>materialist</gloss> spells, nor the materialists themselves, nor does he form friendships with them. He does not associate with <term>Chandalas</term> <gloss>outcastes</gloss>, pugilists, swineherds, poultry-keepers, 
<margin>N 181</margin>
deer-hunters, butchers, actors, dancers, or wrestlers. He does not visit other places of entertainment and play belonging to others, nor does he form friendships with them. Except when they approach him, he speaks the teaching to them from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent on them. 

He does not associate with, resort to, or serve monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who belong to the <term>Shravaka-yana</term> <gloss>the vehicle of the listeners or disciples</gloss>, nor does he form friendships with them. He does not share a common sphere of activity with them, whether in the walking path or the monastery. Except when they approach him, he speaks the teaching to them from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent on them. This, Manjushri, is the sphere of activity of a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva.
<margin>K 277</margin>

Furthermore, Manjushri, a Bodhisattva and Mahasattva does not preach the teaching repeatedly to women by seizing upon signs of affection for one or another of them, nor is he constantly desirous of seeing women. He does not frequently visit families, nor does he think he must constantly speak with girls, maidens, or daughters-in-law, nor does he exchange greetings with them. He does not preach the teaching to a eunuch, nor does he form a friendship with one, nor does he exchange greetings. He does not enter a house alone for the sake of alms, except while maintaining <term>Tathagata-anusmriti</term> <gloss>mindfulness of the Buddha</gloss>. If he does preach the teaching to women, he does so without even the slightest passion for the teaching, much less <note>longing for the women</note>...

<summary>The Buddha instructs Manjushri on the four qualities a Bodhisattva must possess to preach the Lotus Sutra in the future, focusing on proper social conduct and avoiding distracting associations.</summary>
<keywords>Manjushri, Bodhisattva, conduct, sphere of activity, ethics, social avoidance, preaching, Lotus Sutra</keywords>

->13. The Chapter on the Pleasant Abode<-

<margin>K 275 N 180 W 235</margin>
Then <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss>, who is eternally youthful, said to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, it is difficult, extremely difficult, what these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings seeking awakening</gloss> and <term>Mahasattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> have undertaken out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, O Blessed One, should this <term>Dharma-paryaya</term> <gloss>Discourse of the Doctrine</gloss> be proclaimed by these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> and <term>Mahasattvas</term> in the later times, in the final age?"

When this was said, the Blessed One spoke to <term>Manjushri</term>, the youthful: "<term>Manjushri</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> who is established in four qualities should proclaim this <term>Dharma-paryaya</term> in the later times, in the final age. Which four? Here, <term>Manjushri</term>, the <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> should proclaim this <term>Dharma-paryaya</term> in the later times, in the final age, by being established in proper conduct and proper sphere of activity <note>original: "acara-gocara"</note>. And how, <term>Manjushri</term>, is a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> established in proper conduct and sphere of activity?

When a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term>, <term>Manjushri</term>, is patient, gentle, and has reached the stage of self-control; when his mind is not easily frightened or terrified and he is not envious; and when, <term>Manjushri</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> does not dwell upon any phenomena <note>original: "dharmas"</note> but observes the true nature of phenomena according to their own characteristics. That which is the non-upholding and non-conceptualizing of these phenomena is called, <term>Manjushri</term>, the proper conduct of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term>.

And what, <term>Manjushri</term>, is the sphere of activity <note>original: "gocara"</note> of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term>?

<margin>K 276 W 236</margin>
When a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> does not serve kings, does not serve princes, royal ministers, or royal officers; does not associate with, honor, or approach them. He does not associate with, honor, or attend to those of other sects, such as the wandering mendicants <note>original: "carakas"</note>, the religious wanderers <note>original: "parivrajakas"</note>, the <term>Ajivikas</term> <gloss>a fatalist sect</gloss>, or the <term>Nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jains</gloss>; nor those devoted to worldly poetry and literature. He does not serve, honor, or attend to those who hold to the worldly materialistic mantras or the materialists <note>original: "lokayatikas"</note>, nor does he become intimate with them. He does not associate with <term>Chandalas</term> <gloss>outcastes</gloss>, boxers, swineherds, poultry keepers, 

<margin>N 181</margin>
deer hunters, or butchers; nor with actors, dancers, or wrestlers. He does not visit other places of public amusement and play, nor does he become intimate with such people. Unless they approach him, he speaks the <term>Dharma</term> to them only from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent on them. He does not associate with, honor, or attend to monks, nuns, or lay followers who belong to the vehicle of the Disciples <note>original: "shravaka-yana"</note>, nor does he become intimate with them. He does not share a common sphere of activity with them, whether in the walking path or the monastery. Unless they approach him, he speaks the <term>Dharma</term> to them from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent on them. This, <term>Manjushri</term>, is the sphere of activity of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term>.

<margin>K 277</margin>
Furthermore, <term>Manjushri</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> does not frequently teach the <term>Dharma</term> to women by taking hold of signs that arouse desire, nor does he desire to see women frequently. He does not enter the homes of families, nor does he think it proper to speak frequently with young girls, maidens, or daughters-in-law, nor does he engage in polite greetings with them. He does not teach the <term>Dharma</term> to eunuchs, nor does he become intimate with them or greet them politely. He does not enter a house alone for the sake of alms, except when practicing the mindfulness of the <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>the Buddha</gloss>. If he should teach the <term>Dharma</term> to women, he does not teach the <term>Dharma</term> even with a slight affection for the <term>Dharma</term> <note>meaning: he remains detached even from the pleasure of teaching</note>...

<summary>The Buddha instructs Manjushri on the proper conduct and social boundaries required of a Bodhisattva to safely and effectively preach the Lotus Sutra in a future degenerate age. This involves avoiding worldly powers, low-caste professions, and distracting social interactions.</summary>
<keywords>Manjushri, Bodhisattva conduct, sphere of activity, gocara, acara, ethics, social boundaries, monastic discipline</keywords>

->13. The Chapter on the Pleasant Abode<-
<note>original: "१३ सुखविहारपरिवर्तः ।"</note>

<margin>K 275</margin>
N 180
W 235
Then, indeed, <term>Mañjuśrī</term> <gloss>the Youthful Lord</gloss>, the prince, spoke thus to the Lord: "O Lord, it is difficult, O Lord, it is extremely difficult what has been endured by these <term>Bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings dedicated to enlightenment</gloss> <term>Mahāsattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> out of reverence for the Lord. How, O Lord, should this <term>dharmaparyāya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> be proclaimed by these <term>Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas</term> in the final period, in the final time?"

When this was said, the Lord spoke thus to <term>Mañjuśrī</term> <gloss>the Youthful Lord</gloss>, the prince: "A <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> who is established in four things, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, should proclaim this <term>dharmaparyāya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> in the final period, in the final time. In which four? Here, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> established in <term>ācāragocara</term> <gloss>the proper conduct and sphere of activity</gloss> should proclaim this <term>dharmaparyāya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> in the final period, in the final time.

And how, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, does a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> become established in <term>ācāragocara</term> <gloss>proper conduct and sphere of activity</gloss>? When, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> is patient, self-controlled, has reached the stage of the self-controlled, is not terrified <note>alternative: or "undisturbed"</note> in mind, and is not envious; and when, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> does not practice in <note>clarification: or "depend upon"</note> any phenomena <note>alternative: or "laws/things"</note>, but perceives the true nature of phenomena as they really are. Indeed, that which is non-apprehension and non-conceptualization regarding these phenomena, this, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is called the <term>ācāra</term> <gloss>proper conduct</gloss> of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term>.

And what, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is the <term>gocara</term> <gloss>sphere of activity</gloss> of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term>?

<margin>K 276</margin>
W 236
When, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> does not serve the king, does not serve nor associate with nor attend upon nor approach princes, nor royal ministers, nor royal officials; nor does he serve, associate with, or attend upon those of other sects, <term>carakas</term> <gloss>wandering mendicants</gloss>, <term>parivrājakas</term> <gloss>ascetics</gloss>, <term>ājivikas</term> <gloss>determinist ascetics</gloss>, or <term>nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jain ascetics</gloss>, nor beings devoted to poetry and secular treatises; nor does he serve, associate with, or attend upon those who hold the mantras of the <term>lokāyata</term> <gloss>materialists</gloss> nor the materialists themselves, nor does he make acquaintance with them.

Nor <note>clarification: does he associate with</note> <term>caṇḍālas</term> <gloss>outcastes</gloss>, nor boxers, nor pig-breeders, nor poultry-keepers, nor deer-

<margin>N 181</margin>
hunters, nor butchers, nor actors and dancers, nor wrestlers, nor prize-fighters. He does not approach other places of amusement and play belonging to others. Nor does he make acquaintance with them. Except when they have approached <note>clarification: him</note>, he speaks the teaching to them from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent <note>clarification: on them</note>.

And he does not serve, associate with, or attend upon monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who belong to the <term>śrāvakayāna</term> <gloss>vehicle of the disciples</gloss>, nor does he make acquaintance with them. Nor does he have a common sphere of activity with them, whether in the walking-path or in the monastery. Except when they have approached <note>clarification: him</note>, he speaks the teaching to them from time to time, and he speaks it without being dependent. This, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is the <term>gocara</term> <gloss>sphere of activity</gloss> of a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term>.

<margin>K 277</margin>
Furthermore, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</term> does not constantly teach the doctrine to women by seizing upon any sign of affection, nor does he become desirous of constantly seeing women. And he does not approach families <note>clarification: in their homes</note>, nor does he think that a girl, a maiden, or a young woman is someone to be frequently spoken to, nor does he exchange greetings with them. And he does not teach the doctrine to a eunuch, nor does he make acquaintance with him, nor does he exchange greetings with him.

And he does not enter a house alone for the sake of alms, except while practicing <term>tathāgatānuśmṛti</term> <gloss>recollection of the Buddha</gloss>. If he teaches the doctrine to women, he does so without even a passion for the doctrine—not even in the least degree.

---
<margin>
1. G: very difficult.
2. G: omits "in the final period, in the final time."
3. G: omits "not terrified."
4. K: is attached.
5. G: non-conduct in phenomena.
6. G: serves.
7. K: taking, for seizing.
8. G: does not greet.
</margin>

<summary>Mañjuśrī asks the Buddha how Bodhisattvas should preach in the final degenerate age, and the Buddha explains the first of four requirements: established proper conduct and a restricted sphere of activity.</summary>
<keywords>Mañjuśrī, Bodhisattva, conduct, sphere of activity, asceticism, women, final age, teaching methods</keywords>

# 13. The Chapter on Pleasant Practices
<note>original: "सुखविहारपरिवर्तः" (Sukhavihāra-parivarta)</note>

<margin>K 275</margin>
N 180
W 235
Then <term>Mañjuśrī</term> <gloss>the Prince of Dharma</gloss>, who is ever youthful, spoke to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, it is difficult, truly very difficult, for these <term>bodhisattvas</term> <gloss>beings dedicated to enlightenment</gloss> and <term>mahāsattvas</term> <gloss>great beings</gloss> to endure this task out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, O Blessed One, should this <term>dharmaparyāya</term> <gloss>discourse of the teaching</gloss> be proclaimed by these great beings in the final period, in the final age?"

When this was said, the Blessed One spoke to <term>Mañjuśrī</term> the Prince: "By established oneself in four things, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> should proclaim this teaching in the final period, in the final age. Which four? Here, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, the <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term>, being established in proper conduct and spheres of activity, should proclaim this teaching in the final period, in the final age.

And how, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> established in proper conduct and spheres of activity? When, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> is patient, gentle, and has reached the stage of self-control; when his mind is free from alarm, trembling, or fear, and he is not prone to jealousy. When, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> does not dwell on any particular phenomena, but observes the true nature of things as they are. That which is the non-grasping and non-conceptualization of these things is called the proper conduct of a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term>.

<margin>K 276</margin>
W 236
And what, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is the sphere of activity of a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term>? When a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> does not frequent kings, nor does he frequent, serve, attend upon, or approach princes, chief ministers, or royal officers. He does not frequent, serve, or attend upon followers of other sects, such as wandering mendicants, <term>Ajīvikas</term> <gloss>fatalist ascetics</gloss>, or <term>Nirgranthas</term> <gloss>Jain ascetics</gloss>; nor does he frequent those devoted to worldly literature. He does not serve, frequent, or attend upon those who hold materialist spells or followers of materialism, nor does he form close friendships with them.

He does not associate with executioners, or those who keep pigs, poultry, or those who are deer-hunters <margin>N 181</margin> or butchers, nor with dancers, mimes, or wrestlers. He does not frequent other places where people gather for sport and amusement, nor does he form friendships with them. When such people approach him, he preaches the teaching to them from time to time, but he does so without relying on them or seeking anything in return. He does not frequent, serve, or attend upon monks, nuns, or lay followers who belong to the vehicle of the disciples <note>clarification: the Śrāvakayāna</note>, nor does he form friendships with them. He does not share the same sphere of activity with them, whether in walking paths or in monasteries. When they approach him, he preaches the teaching to them from time to time, but he does so without reliance. This, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, is the sphere of activity of a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term>.
<margin>K 277</margin>

Furthermore, <term>Mañjuśrī</term>, a <term>bodhisattva</term> <term>mahāsattva</term> does not frequently teach the Dharma to women by seizing upon signs of attraction, nor does he constantly desire to see women. He does not frequent families, nor does he think it necessary to speak constantly with girls, young women, or daughters-in-law, nor does he exchange greetings of welcome with them. He does not teach the Dharma to eunuchs, nor does he form friendships or exchange greetings with them. He does not enter a house alone for alms, except while practicing <term>tathāgatānusmṛti</term> <gloss>mindfulness of the Buddha</gloss>. If he should teach the Dharma to women, he does not teach the Dharma even with the slightest affection for it—

<summary>The Buddha explains the four pleasant practices or ways of conduct that a bodhisattva must adopt to preach the Lotus Sutra in the degenerate age. This includes maintaining personal integrity through patience and avoiding improper social circles or compromising associations.</summary>
<keywords>Mañjuśrī, bodhisattva, mahāsattva, conduct, sphere of activity, ethics, renunciation, social boundaries, mindfulness of the Buddha</keywords>

<meta>This page is from the Sefer ha-Zohar, Parashat Emor (Folio 104). The layout is a single column of Zoharic text, including a section of the 'Ra'aya Meheimna' (The Faithful Shepherd). The script is Rashi script. The text discusses the spiritual significance of 'Ushpizin' (guests), charity to the poor, and the mystical meaning of the creation of man in the divine image.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

דחזות ליה חולקא בעמיא קדישא יתיר בכלא דמהימנותא לקבלא אושפיזין למחדי בהאי עלמא ובעלמא דאתי. ועבד בעי למחדי למסכני מט' בגין דחולקא דאינון אושפיזין דזמין למסכני הוא וההוא דיתיב בכלא דהמהימנותא ומין אושפיזין אלין עלאין אושפיזין מהימנותא ויהיב לון חולקיהון כלהו קיימי קמיה ואמרי:
> **אל תלחם את לחם רע עין וגו'** <note>משלי כג:ו</note>

השתכח דההוא פתורא דתקין דיליה הוא ולאו דקב"ה עליה כתיב:
> **וזרתי פרש על פניכם וגו' פרש חגיכם וגו'** <note>מלאכי ב:ג</note>

אוי ליה לההוא בר נש בשעתא דאינון אושפיזין מהימנותא קיימי מפתורא. ואמר רבי אבא אברהם כל ימוהי הוה קאים בפרשת אורחין לזמנא אושפיזין ולקבלא לון פתורא השתא דאזמנין ליה ולכלהו צדיקייא ולדוד מלכא ולא יהבין לון חולקהון ההוא קשיא מכולא ואקרי:
> **סורו נא מעל אהלי האנשים הרשעים האלה** <note>במדבר טז:כו</note>

וכלהו סלקין ואמרין: <term>יצחק</term> אמר:
> **ובטן רשעים תחסר** <note>משלי יג:כה</note>

<term>יעקב</term> אמר:
> **פתך אכלת תקיאנה** <note>משלי כג:ח</note>

ושאר כל צדיקייא אמרו:
> **כי כל שלחנות מלאו קיא צואה בלי מקום** <note>ישעיהו כח:ח</note>

<term>דוד מלכא</term> אמר והלכות דיכוי דכתיב ויהי כעפרת הימים וינוף יי' את ככל ומתי מחי קא מיירי בגין דדוד סחל לכבל והתעביד ליה אושפיזא ולא בעא ולא זמין ליה ולא יהב ליה חולקא וכחינון עטרה וימין דדוד מלכא דחין עלמא להלן עלוה ההוא בר נש דאטלים ליה כים יתיר מכלא. אמר ר' אלעזר בנ"כ חסידותא לא פטרת עליה דבר נש יתיר אלא במה דיכול דכתיב ליום כהנתת ידו וגו'. ולא לוחא אינוס חכחא והשבע וארוי קדמיתא ומה דישתאר לתן למסכני אף רוחא דכלא דאושפיזין הוא והיהו לאושפיזין ויהי לון קב"ה חלי עמיה ולברכה קרי עליה:
> **אז תתענג על יי' וגו'** <note>ישעיהו נח:יד</note>

ויצחק קארי עליה:
> **כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח** <note>ישעיהו נד:יז</note>

אמר רבי שמעון האי דוד מלכא א"ל בגין דכל זינין דמלכא וקרבין למלכא בידוי דדוד אתפקדו. חכ"ז מאן דחדי גבור בחלקו ורעו וגו' קטן ועיסר כביט וגו' יעקב אמר לו ויבקע בבקר חורך וגו' שאר צדיקייא אמרו וכהך יי' תמיד והשביע וגו'. דוד מלכא אמר כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח דהוא על כל זיני זינין אתפקד וכלה חולקיה דבר נש זכי לכל האי זכחן חולקיהון דצדיקייא בעלמא דין ובעלמא דאתי עליהו כתיב:
> **ועמך כלם צדיקים וגו'** <note>ישעיהו ס:כא</note>

---

### רעיא מהימנא (The Faithful Shepherd)

-> **ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו'** <- <note>ויקרא כג:מ</note>

**פקודא** דא ליטול לולב כדקא יאות ביומין אלין ויהי נמיכין וזיין ליה וקאי רזא דאוקימנא ולקחתם פדירוס כמה דקב"ה נטיל לון לישראל בהאי זימנא דדינון. אוף הכי ופרש בעיין ליה לקב"ה בחולקהון וחלוסן ביה. ולפ' קדמא דא לולב וזמין דכיה למיסב רזא דיוקנא דאדם וכן למטה. עב'.

הבקרח סמאי לככולי ברחמיו ובדתיו אף עשותיו. כל הבקרח סמיאי דא אדם דקב"ה קארי ליה סמאי דכתי' ויברא אלהים את האדם בצלמו ועוד דחקרי בבמיה בשעתא דחפיק קשוט וזיחא בעלמא וחקרי אלהים דכתיב אלהים לא תקלל קרא ליה בבמיה דכתיב ויברא אלהים

---

את האדם בצלמו ושפיר קא לוקימנא דכתיב **נעשה אדם בצלמנו כדמותנו** בשעתא דזווגא אתמר. וכך הוא כוונא דתרוייהו בנלס ודמות וחדס דדכר ונוקבא נפק ויברא אלהים את האדם בצלמו. כפכח דסליק מלכא אשכחנא דבשעתא דזווגא השתכח.

[context] The second “dwell” refers to human beings;
for he who has a portion in the holy land and people sits in the shadow of faith to receive the guests so as to rejoice in this world and the next. He must also gladden the poor, because the portion of those guests whom he invites must go to the poor. And if a man sits in the shadow of faith and invites these guests and does not give them their portion, they all hold aloof from him, saying “Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye” (Prov. 23, 6). That table which he prepares is his own and not God’s. Alas for him when those guests leave his table.
R. Abba further said: ‘Abraham always used to stand at the cross roads to invite guests to his table. Now when a man invites him and all the righteous and King David and does not give them their portion, Abraham rises from the table and exclaims, “Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men” (Num. 16, 26), and all rise and follow him. Isaac says, “The belly of the wicked shall want” (Prov. 13, 26). Jacob says, “The morsel thou hast eaten thou shalt vomit up” (Ibid. 23, 8). The other righteous ones say, “For all tables are full of vomit and uncleanness” (Isa. 28, 8).
David says: [lacuna] In those ten days during which David judges the world, that man is judged who has treated him more ungratefully than Nabal.’
R. Eleazar said: ‘The Torah does not demand of a man more than he can perform, as it says, “Each one man shall give as he is able,’ (Deut. 16, 7). A man should not say, I will first satisfy myself with food and drink, and what is left I shall give to the poor, but the first of everything must be for the guests. And if he gladdens the guests and satisfies them, God rejoices with him and Abraham proclaims over him, “Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord”, etc. (Isa. 58, 14). Isaac proclaims, “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper” (Ibid. 54, 17).’ R. Simeon said: ‘This verse is said by King David, because all royal weapons of war have been handed to David. What Isaac says is, “His seed shall be mighty on the earth” (Ps. 112, 2).
Jacob proclaims, “Then shall thy light break forth as the morning” (Isa. 58, 8). The other righteous say, “The Lord shall guide thee continually and satisfy thy soul in dry places” (Ibid. 11). Happy the lot of the man who attains ta all this!’ AND YE SHALL TAKE YOU ON THE FIRST DAY THE FRUIT OF GOODLY TREES.
R. Simeon quoted here the verse: “Every one that is called by my name, for my glory I have created him, I have formed him, yea I have made him” (Isa. 63, 7). ‘ “Every one that is called by my name”: this is man whom God has created in His likeness and whom He calls by His own name when he does truth and justice, as it is written, “Thou shalt not revile the judges” (Elohim, Ex. 22, 28).
“I have formed him, yea I have made him”: as has been explained, the words “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” refer to the time of wedlock, namely, the union of “image” and “likeness”, so that man issued from Male and Female.
In the Book of King Solomon it is written that at the hour of wedded union on earth,
[context] God sends a certain form with the figure of a human being which hovers over the union, and if a man’s eye were capable of such a thing it would see such a form over his head.

Whoever has a portion in the holy people must show greater faith than all others by welcoming the <term>ushpizin</term> <gloss>sacred guests</gloss> to rejoice in this world and the world to come. A person should make the poor rejoice, because the portion of food intended for those guests belongs to the poor. One who sits within the wholeness of faith and invites these supreme guests, the guests of faith, and gives them their portion, they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of a stingy man...** <note>Proverbs 23:6. The original Hebrew implies a "bad eye," referring to one who is ungenerous.</note>

It turns out that the table such a person prepared belongs to himself and not to the Holy One, blessed be He. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices...** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those guests of faith rise from his table. Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and set a table for them. Now that they invite him <note>as a spiritual guest during the festival of Sukkot</note> along with all the righteous and King David, and people do not give them their portion <note>by feeding the poor</note>, it is the hardest thing of all. About this it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **The morsel which you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the rest of the righteous say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>King David</term> spoke of the laws of oppression <note>The OCR text is somewhat fragmented here; it refers to the spiritual exile and rejection David feels when not properly hosted</note>... because David was the last of the guests and was made a guest, but the host did not desire him, did not invite him, and gave him no portion. Since King David represents the <term>Crown</term> <gloss>Malchut/Kingship</gloss> and the Right Hand <note>the sefirah of Chesed</note>, that person who deprives him pushes the world away. Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not required to do more than they are able, as it is written, "each according to the gift of his hand." One should not say: "I will eat and satisfy myself first, and what remains I will give to the poor." Rather, the first of everything belongs to the guests. If he makes the guests rejoice, the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, and Isaac calls out a blessing over him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And <note>the text attributes this to Isaac elsewhere</note> says:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper.** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimeon said: King David said this because all the weapons and wars of the King are entrusted into David's hands. Happy is the one who rejoices in his portion. Jacob said of him, "Then your light shall break forth as the morning." Other righteous ones said, "The Lord shall guide you continually and satisfy your soul." King David said, "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of weapons. This is the portion of the person who merits all these merits. Concerning the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, it is written:
> **And your people shall all be righteous...** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd <note>original: Ra'aya Meheimna</note>

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

This **commandment** <note>original: pikuda</note> is to take the <term>lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> properly during these days... This is the secret of what we have established: "And you shall take" <note>the word "take" in Hebrew can be rearranged to hint at a "precious fruit"</note>. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time of judgment, so should people seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion. The <term>lulav</term> is invited to represent the mystery of the "Image of Man" <note>Adam</note> and so it is below.

<unclear>The text here is highly fragmented in the OCR, discussing the name of God and the creation of man</unclear>. The Holy One, blessed be He, called him "Man" <note>Adam</note>, as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." And he is called by the name "Elohim" <gloss>God/Judge</gloss> as it is written: "You shall not revile Elohim." 

---

...Man in His image. And it is well explained by the verse: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.** This was said at the time of the union <note>the mystical union of the divine masculine and feminine</note>. Thus, the intention of both "Image" and "Likeness" refers to the male and female coming forth as one. "And God created man in His image" — when the King ascends, we find that it was found at the time of the union.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical significance of hosting the seven "ushpizin" (spiritual guests) during Sukkot, emphasizing that their portion must be given to the poor. It also introduces a section from the Faithful Shepherd regarding the Lulav and the creation of humanity in the divine image (Tzelem).</summary>

<keywords>Ushpizin, Sukkot, charity, King David, Lulav, Divine Image, Tzelem, Ra'aya Meheimna, creation of man</keywords>

<meta>This page corresponds to Folio 104 of the Zohar on Parashat Emor. It discusses the mystical hospitality of the Sukkot festival, focusing on the Ushpizin (holy guests) and the spiritual consequences of neglecting the poor. The lower section contains the Ra’aya Meheimna (Faithful Shepherd) commentary on the Four Species and the creation of man.</meta>

## Main Text

A person’s portion within the holy nation is recognized most through faith by receiving <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>sacred guests</gloss> to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. A person must cause the poor to rejoice, for the portion of those <term>Ushpizin</term> whom he invites belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these supernal <term>Ushpizin</term>, the guests of faith, but does not give them their portion <note>by failing to feed the poor who represent them</note>, they all stand over him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye...** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own and not the Holy One, blessed be He’s. Regarding such a person it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices...** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those <term>Ushpizin</term> of faith rise from his table. Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and set a table for them. Now, when the poor invite him <note>Abraham</note> and all the righteous ones and King David, and people do not give them their portion, it is the hardest thing of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men.** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Yitzchak</term> <gloss>Isaac</gloss> says:
> **...but the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Yaakov</term> <gloss>Jacob</gloss> says:
> **The morsel which you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of filthy vomit, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

<term>David Malka</term> <gloss>King David</gloss> spoke of the laws of being crushed <note>oppressed by poverty</note>... <unclear>for David became a guest and was not desired, nor invited, nor given a portion</unclear>. Because King David is the Crown <note>the Sefirah of Malchut</note> and the right hand <note>Chesed</note>, a person who withholds from him causes more damage than any other. Rabbi Eleazar said: A person is not exempt from the duty of kindness except by what he is able to do, as it is written: "according to the gift of his hand." He should not overextend himself, but should first eat and satisfy himself, and what remains should be given to the poor. This is the spirit of the guests, and the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells with him. To bless him, He calls over him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls over him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper.** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This is what King David said because all the weapons and battles of the King are entrusted to the hands of David. Happy is the one who rejoices <unclear>in his portion and his will</unclear>. Jacob said to him: "Then shall your light break forth as the morning." The other righteous ones said: "And the Lord shall guide you continually and satisfy your soul." King David said: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of weapons. When a person merits all these merits, the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come is written regarding them:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous...** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

***

### The Faithful Shepherd

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <note>Leviticus 23:40</note> <-

This **commandment** is to take the <term>Lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is fitting in these days... and it stands as a mystery that we have established: "And you shall take" <note>Hebrew: u-lekachtem</note> is like "taking a bride," for the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they must seek the Holy One, blessed be He, in their portion and cleave to Him. This first commandment is the <term>Lulav</term>, which is ready to take up the mystery of the Image of Man <note>the Anthropos or Adam Kadmon</note> below.

<unclear>Regarding the Name of God in His mercy and His attributes...</unclear> All these are "Man," whom the Holy One, blessed be He, calls by the Name, as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, He is called by the name <term>Elohim</term> <gloss>God/Judge</gloss> at the time when truth and radiance emerge in the world. It is written, "You shall not revile Elohim," and regarding Man it is written: "And God <note>Elohim</note> created

***

man in His own image." And we have well established that it is written: **Let us make man in our image, after our likeness.** At the time of the union <note>of the divine male and female principles</note> it was said. And such is the intention of both: "Image" and "Likeness" refer to the male and female that emerged. "And God created man in His own image." When the King ascends, we find that at the time of the union He is found.

A person who sees their portion in the holy people has superiority in all matters of faith <note>original: "מהימנותא"</note>, to receive the guests <note>term: ushpizin</note> <gloss>spiritual guests, the seven founding fathers of Israel</gloss> and to rejoice in this world and the world to come. And a person must give joy to the poor, for the portion of these guests whom he invites belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these exalted guests, the guests of faith, but does not give them their portion <note>clarification: by failing to feed the poor</note>, they all stand over him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

> **I will spread dung upon your faces, etc., the dung of your festivals, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person at the time when these guests of faith rise from his table. Now that people invite him, and all the righteous ones, and King David <note>term: David Malka</note>, yet do not give them their portion, this is the hardest matter of all and is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: Isaac <note>term: Yitzhak</note> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

Jacob <note>term: Yaakov</note> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the rest of the righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

This refers to one who causes David to suffer, making him a guest but failing to invite him <note>clarification: to the meal</note> or give him his portion. Since the Crown <note>term: Atarah</note> <gloss>the tenth Sephirah, Malchut</gloss> and the Right Hand <note>clarification: the Sephirah of Chesed</note> are the strength of King David, that person who harms him is pushed further away than anyone. A man should not feel coerced, but should eat and satisfy himself first, and what remains should be given to the poor. Indeed, the spirit of all the guests is there, and they are guests for him. The Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him and calls a blessing upon him:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And Isaac calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper.** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimeon said: This King David said it because all the armaments of the King and the King's battles are entrusted into David's hands. Therefore, whoever rejoices in his portion and will <unclear>...</unclear>. Jacob said to him: "Then shall your light break forth as the morning, etc." The rest of the righteous said: "And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul, etc." King David said: "No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all kinds of armaments. This is the portion of a person who merits all these merits. Regarding the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, it is written:
> **And your people shall all be righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion. Furthermore, he is called by His name <note>clarification: Elohim</note> at the time he brings truth and <unclear>...</unclear> into the world. the man in His image." And we have well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"** which was said at the time of union <note>clarification: the mystical coupling of the divine attributes</note>. For he has a portion in the holy people, more so than all, in the faith <note>clarification: the power of faith</note> to receive guests and to rejoice in this world and the world to come. A person must cause the poor to rejoice, because the portion of those guests <term>Ushpizin</term> <gloss>mystical celestial guests</gloss> who are invited belongs to the poor. One who sits in the wholeness of faith and invites these exalted guests, the guests of faith, but does not give them their portion <note>clarification: by failing to feed the poor</note>, they all stand over him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of one who has an evil eye...** <note>original: "אל תלחם את לחם רע עין וגו'" (Proverbs 23:6)</note>

It turns out that the table he prepared is his own and not the Holy One’s, blessed be He. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festivals...** <note>original: "וזרתי פרש על פניכם וגו' פרש חגיכם וגו'" (Malachi 2:3)</note>

Woe to that person at the time when those guests of faith rise from the table. Rabbi Abba said: All the days of Abraham, he would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and receive them at his table. Now that people invite him <note>context: as a mystical guest during the festival of Sukkot</note> and all the righteous ones and King David, but do not give them their portion, it is the hardest thing of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men...** <note>original: "סורו נא מעל אהלי האנשים הרשעים האלה" (Numbers 16:26)</note>

And they all ascend and say: <term>Yitzhak</term> <gloss>Isaac</gloss> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>original: "ובטן רשעים תחסר" (Proverbs 13:25)</note>

<term>Ya'akov</term> <gloss>Jacob</gloss> says:
> **The morsel you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>original: "פתך אכלת תקיאנה" (Proverbs 23:8)</note>

And all the other righteous ones say:
> **For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no place clean.** <note>original: "כי כל שלחנות מלאו קיא צואה בלי מקום" (Isaiah 28:8)</note>

<term>David Malka</term> <gloss>King David</gloss> spoke of the laws of oppression, for David suffered and made himself a guest, yet the man did not desire him, did not invite him, and did not give him his portion. And since the crown and the right hand of King David sustain the world, that man who robs him causes more damage than any other. Rabbi Elazar said: A person is not exempt from acts of kindness <term>hasiduta</term> <gloss>piety/loving-kindness</gloss> except according to what they are able, as it is written "according to the gift of his hand." First, one should satisfy and gladden themselves, and what remains should be given to the poor; this is the very spirit of the guests. The Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with them and calls out a blessing:
> **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** <note>original: "אז תתענג על יי' וגו'" (Isaiah 58:14)</note>

And Isaac calls out over him:
> **No weapon formed against you shall prosper.** <note>original: "כל כלי יוצר עליך לא יצלח" (Isaiah 54:17)</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: King David said this because all the armaments of the King and the battles of the King are entrusted into the hands of David. Happy is the one who rejoices in his portion. Jacob said of him: "Then your light shall break forth as the morning." The other righteous ones said: "And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy your soul." King David said: "No weapon formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all types of armaments. This is the portion of a person who merits all these merits. Regarding the portion of the righteous in this world and the world to come, it is written:
> **And your people shall all be righteous...** <note>original: "ועמך כלם צדיקים וגו'" (Isaiah 60:21)</note>

---

### The Faithful Shepherd <note>original: "רעיא מהימנא" (Ra'aya Meheimna)</note>

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day...** <- <note>original: "ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון וגו'" (Leviticus 23:40)</note>

This **commandment** <term>pikuda</term> is to take the <term>lulav</term> <gloss>palm branch</gloss> as is proper during these days. This contains a secret: just as the Holy One, blessed be He, took Israel at this time of judgment, so too must they seek the Holy One as their portion and take hold of Him. The first of these is the palm branch, which represents the secret of the image of Adam <note>clarification: the primordial man</note>.

The Holy One, blessed be He, created Adam in His image, as it is written: "And God created man in His own image." Furthermore, he is called "Elohim" <note>clarification: a title of authority/divinity</note> at the time when truth and radiance emerge in the world. It is written: "You shall not revile God <term>Elohim</term>," referring to his greatness, for it is written: "And God created 

---

man in His image." And it has been well established that it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"** which was said at the time of the union <note>clarification: the mystical union of divine attributes</note>. Such is the intention of both, "image" <term>tselem</term> and "likeness" <term>demut</term>, representing the male and female that emerged together. "And God created man in His own image." We find that when the King ascends, it occurs at the time of the union.

It also begins a discourse from the 'Faithful Shepherd' on the commandment of the Lulav and the creation of man in the divine image.</summary>

When with the palatable food he'd done, the king sought wine, began a joyous bout.
When sundry cups of wine the king had drunk, the perspiration started from his brow.
He said, O host, who own (this) golden house, your place is pleasant, and your means are good.
But this high palace (here) of sixty steps, around whose head the sky its lasso whirls, —
When sixty years have now passed over you, how can you walk up to the top of it?
The officer replied, The King live aye! His wine be Kausar, huris give the cup!
This is in me no wonder, I'm a man; how should I (then) be wearied by such steps?
The wonder this, that there's a moon-like girl, soft, dainty as the king's ermine and silk.
Who puts a mount-like ox upon her back, and brings it hither at the feeding-time.
She bears it sixty steps up at a stretch, not resting (on the way) at any step.
An ox! What ox? An elephant, a load which ne'er an elephant would bear a mile.
God witness! in this land no one could (lift and) poise it for a moment from the ground.
Then (if) a woman bears it to a height of sixty steps, is it not marvellous?
After the officer had told this tale, the king bit with his teeth his finger-tips.
He said, How can a thing of this kind be? It cannot; if it be, 'tis sorcery.
This business I, in truth, shall not believe, until with my own eyes I see it (done).
Then of (his) host, (the officer), he asked that he should prove the claim his words set forth.
The host heard this; he went below and told to her who bore the ox the lion's case.

When the King had finished the delicious foods, he set the wine flowing and arranged a banquet of joy.
When the King had drunk two or three goblets of wine, a sweat broke out upon his rose-colored forehead.
He said: "O host of the golden palace, your dwelling is pleasant and your provisions are ample."
"But these sixty steps of this high palace, over whose summit the heavens pass like a lasso,"
"After sixty years have passed you by, how can you traverse them beneath your feet?"
The host replied: "May the King remain eternal, may his wine be from the spring of <term>Kawsar</term> <gloss>a river in Paradise</gloss> and his cupbearer a <term>Houri</term> <gloss>celestial maiden</gloss>."
"This is no wonder for me, for I am a man; how could I ever grow weary of such steps?"
"The wonder is that there is a girl like the moon, as soft and delicate as the King's silk and ermine."
"She takes a bull as heavy as a mountain upon her neck and brings it to the place of feeding."
"She climbs the sixty steps in one breath, without pausing to rest on any stair."
"And what a bull! It is like an elephant; even a mile-long journey would not tire its fat."
"By God, if anyone else in this land could even lift it for a single breath from the ground,"
"How then could a woman carry it up a sixty-step fortress? Is this not a wondrous thing?"
When the <term>Sarhang</term> <gloss>officer or host</gloss> told this tale to the King, the King bit his fingertip in amazement.
He said: "How can a deed of this kind be? If it is not impossible, it must be magic."
"I cannot truly believe this tale until I see it with my own eyes first."
Then he requested of the host that he prove the claim of his words to be true.
When the host heard this, he went down and told the Lion’s <note>the King's</note> story to the one who carries the bull.

“After judging among the teachings,”

Seeing views without adopting any,
searching, I saw inner peace.”
“O sage, you speak of judgments you have formed,”
said Māgaṇḍiya,

# The Chapter of the Octads <note>original: "Atthakavagga"</note>

836. "If you do not desire such a jewel," <note>Māgandiya refers to his daughter, whom he offered to the Buddha</note> "a woman sought after by many lords of men, then what kind of view, what conduct and vows, and what rebirth in a future existence do you proclaim?" <margin>2.</margin>

837. "Māgandiya," said the Blessed One <note>original: "Bhagavā"</note>, "I do not say 'I proclaim this' regarding things reached by making a definitive judgment among various doctrines. Looking among the different views, but not grasping them, I searched for and saw inner peace <note>original: "ajjhattasanti"</note>." <margin>3.</margin>

838. "Those fixed conclusions that have been constructed," said Māgandiya, "you say you do not grasp them, O Sage <note>original: "muni"</note>. This matter you call 'inner peace,' how is that explained by the wise?" <margin>4.</margin>

839. "Māgandiya," said the Blessed One, "one does not speak of purity <note>original: "suddhi"</note> by means of views, or by what is heard, or by knowledge, or even by conduct and vows. Nor is purity achieved by the absence of views, the absence of hearing, the absence of knowledge, or the absence of conduct and vows. Letting go of these without grasping, being at peace and independent, one would not crave for renewed existence." <margin>5.</margin>

840. "If, as you say, one does not speak of purification <note>original: "visuddhi"</note> by means of views, or by what is heard, or by knowledge," said Māgandiya, "or even by conduct and vows..."

<summary>This page contains a dialogue from the Magandiya Sutta where the Buddha rejects the notion of finding spiritual purity through dogmatic views, rituals, or sensory knowledge, pointing instead to inner peace.</summary>

# The Octad Chapter <note>original: "Atthakavagga"</note>

836. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note>
If you do not desire such a jewel as this,
a woman sought after by many lords of men,
then what kind of view, what conduct and vows,
and what rebirth in existence do you proclaim?

837. <note>The Blessed One </note><note>original: "Bhagavā"</note> speaks:
Māgandiya, for such a person there is no thought of "I proclaim this,"
regarding the teachings <note>original: "dhammesu"</note> that are grasped after making a firm judgment.
Seeing the various views, but not grasping them,
while searching for inward peace <note>original: "ajjhattasanti"</note>, I saw the truth.

838. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note>
Those judgments which have been fashioned,
O Sage <note>original: "muni"</note>, you say you do not grasp them.
This thing called "inward peace,"
how is that explained by the wise?

839. <note>The Blessed One speaks:</note>
Māgandiya, one does not speak of purity <note>original: "suddhi"</note> by means of views,
nor by learning, nor by knowledge, nor by conduct and vows.
Yet one does not say purity is attained through the absence of views,
through the absence of learning, through the absence of knowledge,
nor through the lack of conduct or vows.
Having let go of these without grasping,
at peace and independent, one would not long for becoming <note>original: "bhavaṃ"</note>.

840. <note>Māgandiya speaks:</note>
If, as you say, one does not speak of purity by views,
nor by learning, nor by knowledge,
nor even by conduct and vows...

<summary>The Buddha explains to the Brahmin Māgandiya that spiritual purity is not achieved through intellectual views or external rituals, but through inward peace and non-attachment. He clarifies that while rituals and views are not the cause of purity, one should not simply embrace ignorance either.</summary>

But seeing <note>clarification: the danger</note> in views without grasping <note>original: "anuggahāya"</note>, searching for <note>original: "pacinaṃ"</note> inner peace <note>original: "ajjhattasantiṃ"</note>, I saw <note>clarification: the truth</note>."

838. "Those judgments which have been fashioned," said Māgandiya, "you, Sage <note>original: "muni"</note>, speak of them without grasping. This matter which is called 'inner peace,' how indeed is that made known by the wise?"

839. "Not by view, not by tradition <note>original: "sutiyā"</note>, not by knowledge," said the Blessed One to Māgandiya, "and even by conduct and vows <note>original: "sīlabbatenāpi"</note>, one does not attain purity <note>original: "suddhim"</note>. Having abandoned these <note>clarification: extremes</note> without grasping, peaceful <note>original: "santo"</note> and independent <note>original: "anissāya"</note>, one should not long for existence."

840. "If indeed you say that not by view, not by tradition, not by knowledge," said Māgandiya, "and even by conduct and vows, one does not attain purity..."
